edit.title: Hisab Class One
edit.mDescription:
A Class 1 mathematics textbook in Rohingya, written in the Hanifi script. It teaches the numbers 0 to 10 with their Rohingya names, counting with pictures, and first comparisons such as many and few or big and small.
Writer        : Zuban Committee
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 34
File Size     : 8.9 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Zubanor Hisab
edit.mDescription:
A picture book that introduces young children to the Hanifi Rohingya numerals. Each number has a short illustrated sentence to count along with, followed by writing practice.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 26
File Size     : 3.1 MB

edit.title: Rohingyas and Kamans
edit.mDescription:
A short history of two Muslim communities of Arakan, the Rohingya and the Kaman, by the historian M. A. Tahir Ba Tha, compiled from his earlier magazine articles. It was distributed by the United Rohingya National League in Myitkyina.

ရခိုင်ပြည်ရှိ မွတ်စလင်လူမျိုးစု နှစ်စုဖြစ်သော ရိုဟင်ဂျာနှင့် ကမန်လူမျိုးတို့၏ သမိုင်းကို သမိုင်းပညာရှင် အမ်.အေ. တာဟီရ်ဘသာ ရေးသားထားသော စာအုပ်ငယ်ဖြစ်သည်။ စာရေးသူ၏ ယခင် မဂ္ဂဇင်းဆောင်းပါးများကို စုစည်းထားပြီး မြစ်ကြီးနားမြို့ ရိုဟင်ဂျာအမျိုးသားညီညွတ်ရေးအဖွဲ့ (U.R.N.L.) က ဖြန့်ဝေခဲ့သည်။
Author        : M. A. Tahir Ba Tha
Year          : 1963
Language      : Burmese
Publisher     : United Rohingya National League (U.R.N.L.), Myitkyina
Pages         : 44
File Size     : 2.0 MB

edit.title: ရိုဟင်ဂျာသမိုင်းကိုဆန်းစစ်ခြင်း
edit.mDescription:
"Examining Rohingya History" by U Kyaw Min, elected to parliament for Buthidaung in 1990. Chapters cover a chronology of Arakan, who the Rohingya are, the claim that they came from a neighbouring country, the "white card" registration, and multicultural Mrauk-U; the author argues that the Rohingya are an original people of Arakan. Written in 2002 and published as a book after his release from prison in 2012.

၁၉၉၀ ပြည့်နှစ် ရွေးကောက်ပွဲတွင် ဘူးသီးတောင်မြို့နယ်မှ လွှတ်တော်ကိုယ်စားလှယ်အဖြစ် ရွေးကောက်ခံခဲ့သူ ဦးကျော်မင်းက ရိုဟင်ဂျာသမိုင်းကို ဆန်းစစ်ထားသော စာအုပ်ဖြစ်သည်။ ရခိုင်သမိုင်းစဉ်ဆက်၊ ရိုဟင်ဂျာ ဘယ်သူလဲ၊ အဖြူကတ် (White Card) နှင့် ယဉ်ကျေးမှုစုံလင်သော မြောက်ဦး စသည့် အခန်းများ ပါဝင်ပြီး ရိုဟင်ဂျာများသည် ရခိုင်ပြည်၏ မူလလူမျိုးတစ်မျိုး ဖြစ်ကြောင်း စာရေးသူက တင်ပြထားသည်။ ၂၀၀၂ ခုနှစ်က ရေးသားခဲ့ပြီး ၂၀၁၂ ခုနှစ် ထောင်မှ လွတ်မြောက်ပြီးနောက် စာအုပ်အဖြစ် ထုတ်ဝေခဲ့သည်။
Author        : U Kyaw Min
Language      : Burmese
Pages         : 150
File Size     : 12.8 MB

edit.title: I still don't feel safe to go home
edit.mDescription:
An Oxfam briefing paper in which Rohingya refugees in the Cox's Bazar camps describe the violence that drove them from Myanmar, life in overcrowded camps, and their fear of being sent back without safety, citizenship and equal rights. Published in December 2017, when more than 626,000 people had fled since 25 August.
Author        : Edmund Cairns (Oxfam)
Year          : 2017
Language      : English
Publisher     : Oxfam GB for Oxfam International
ISBN          : 978-1-78748-146-6
Pages         : 20
File Size     : 1.9 MB

edit.title: Bob Rae's Final Report on Rohingya
edit.mDescription:
The final report of Bob Rae, Canada's Special Envoy to Myanmar, based on his research and visits from October 2017 to March 2018. It covers the humanitarian crisis in Bangladesh and Myanmar, Myanmar's politics, the evidence of crimes against humanity, and ends with 17 recommendations for Canada and the international community.
Author        : Bob Rae
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Publisher     : Government of Canada
Pages         : 30
File Size     : 7.6 MB

edit.title: 1983 Burma population Census-Book
edit.mDescription:
The national ("Burma") volume of the 1983 Population Census of the Socialist Republic of the Union of Burma, taken on 1–5 April 1983. Part one reports the main findings, the sample design and the post-enumeration check; part two has 38 tables on the population, households, and social and economic characteristics.
Author        : Immigration and Manpower Department
Year          : 1986
Language      : English
Pages         : 271
File Size     : 12.3 MB

edit.title: Dunno Sahir Hottor Hadis
edit.mDescription:
Seventy hadith from Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, each given in Arabic with a Rohingya translation in the Hanifi script and its source.
Language      : Arabic and Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 16
File Size     : 6.8 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Hoax
edit.mDescription:
Maung Tha Hla argues that the Rohingya are not an indigenous people of Arakan but descendants of migrants from Chittagong, presents Rohingya movements as linked to Islamist militancy and a threat to Burma's national security, and disputes Rohingya accounts of their origins.
Author        : Maung Tha Hla
Year          : 2009
Language      : English
Publisher     : Buddhist Rakhaing Cultural Association, New York
ISBN          : 0-9726465-1-5
Pages         : 108
File Size     : 17.9 MB

edit.title: Universal Declaration of Human Right in Burmese
edit.mDescription:
The full text of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948, in the Burmese translation published by the UN human rights office.

၁၉၄၈ ခုနှစ် ဒီဇင်ဘာလ ၁၀ ရက်နေ့တွင် ကုလသမဂ္ဂ အထွေထွေညီလာခံက အတည်ပြုခဲ့သော အပြည်ပြည်ဆိုင်ရာ လူ့အခွင့်အရေး ကြေညာစာတမ်း၏ မြန်မာဘာသာပြန် စာသားအပြည့်အစုံ ဖြစ်သည်။ ကုလသမဂ္ဂ လူ့အခွင့်အရေးရုံး ထုတ်ပြန်ထားသော ဘာသာပြန်ကို ကူးယူထားခြင်း ဖြစ်သည်။
Author        : United Nations General Assembly
Year          : 1948
Language      : Burmese
Publisher     : UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights
Pages         : 8
File Size     : 0.1 MB

edit.title: မြန်မာ့စွယ်စုံကျမ်း အတွဲ (၉) အပိုင်း (က)
edit.mDescription:
Volume 9, Part A of the Myanmar Encyclopedia (Myanma Swezon Kyan), the Burmese-language general encyclopedia compiled by the Burma Translation Society (Sarpay Beikman) in Rangoon and first printed in 1964. It has alphabetical entries from Mahaw to U Maung Gyi on Burmese and world subjects, such as the Mahosadha Jataka, Mussolini and Mexico, with photographs and maps. It opens with a guide to using the encyclopedia and its alphabetical order.

မြန်မာနိုင်ငံ ဘာသာပြန်စာပေအသင်း (စာပေဗိမာန်) က ပြုစုထုတ်ဝေသော မြန်မာ့စွယ်စုံကျမ်း အတွဲ ၉၊ အပိုင်း (က) ဖြစ်ပြီး ၁၉၆၄ ခုနှစ်တွင် ပထမအကြိမ် ပုံနှိပ်ခဲ့သည်။ "မဟော" မှ "ဦးမောင်ကြီး" အထိ အက္ခရာစဉ်အလိုက် ခေါင်းစဉ်များ ပါဝင်ပြီး မဟောသဓဇာတ်တော်၊ မူဆိုလီနီ၊ မက္ကဆီကိုနိုင်ငံ စသည့် မြန်မာနှင့် ကမ္ဘာ့အကြောင်းအရာများကို ဓာတ်ပုံများ၊ မြေပုံများဖြင့် ရှင်းပြထားသည်။ စာအုပ်အစတွင် စွယ်စုံကျမ်းကို အသုံးပြုပုံနှင့် အက္ခရာစဉ်ဇယား ပါဝင်သည်။
Author        : Burma Translation Society
Editor        : U Myat Soe
Year          : 1964
Language      : Burmese
Publisher     : Burma Translation Society (Sarpay Beikman), Rangoon
Pages         : 261
File Size     : 7.5 MB

edit.title: A Bachelor Girl in Burma
edit.mDescription:
A light, personal travel account by G. E. Mitton, a young unmarried Englishwoman who visited Burma, published in London in 1907. She describes Rangoon and the Shwe Dagon Pagoda, the home life of Burmese women, Moulmein, Mandalay, and journeys north towards Bhamo and the China road through the Irrawaddy defiles, as well as pwe performances and a trip on a cargo boat. It has 95 illustrations from photographs, mostly taken by the author.
Author        : G. E. Mitton
Year          : 1907
Language      : English
Publisher     : Adam and Charles Black, London
Pages         : 403
File Size     : 10.0 MB

edit.title: A Burmese Loneliness: A Tale of Travel in Burma, the Southern Shan States and Keng Tung
edit.mDescription:
A travel book by Captain C. M. Enriquez, an Indian Army officer serving with the Burma Military Police, published in Calcutta in 1918. Written during a lonely posting at Keng Tung in the Southern Shan States, it describes the town's festivals, market and shrines, the Shan people, Loimwe, and the frontiers with French Indo-China along the Mekong, Siam and China. Later chapters cover local arts and industries and the author's thoughts on Burma. It has a map and illustrations.
Author        : C. M. Enriquez
Year          : 1918
Language      : English
Publisher     : Thacker, Spink & Co., Calcutta
Pages         : 384
File Size     : 13.6 MB

edit.title: A Burmese Wonderland: A Tale of Travel in Lower and Upper Burma
edit.mDescription:
A travel book by Major C. M. Enriquez of the Kachin Rifles, published in Calcutta in 1922, mixing travel with history and folklore. Book One covers Lower Burma — the Kyaik-hti-yo pagoda, Thaton, the Talaings (Mon) and Karens, the Salween River, Tenasserim and Arakan. Book Two covers Upper Burma — the Pyu, Pagan and King Kyanzittha, Mount Popa and the Lower Chindwin, with chapters on General Bandula, Burmese military history, Buddhism, the old monarchy and the country beyond Mandalay.
Author        : C. M. Enriquez
Year          : 1922
Language      : English
Publisher     : Thacker, Spink & Co., Calcutta and Simla
Pages         : 324
File Size     : 13.8 MB

edit.title: A Civil Servant in Burma
edit.mDescription:
The memoir of Sir Herbert Thirkell White, who spent more than thirty years in the Burma civil service and became its Lieutenant-Governor, published in London in 1913. He tells of official life from the late 1870s, service on the frontier, the British capture of Mandalay in 1885 and the first years after the annexation of Upper Burma, a visit to the Shan States, a boundary commission and his last years on the Chief Court. There are also chapters on Burmese life and character and on Buddhism, with photographs, a glossary and an index.
Author        : Sir Herbert Thirkell White
Year          : 1913
Language      : English
Publisher     : Edward Arnold, London

A Burmese history by the researcher U Maung Maung Gyi (Mann) of the Muslims who are nationals of Burma and their part in the country's national life. It describes how Islam reached Burma, the indigenous Muslim groups - the Rohingya, Kaman, Panthay, Pashu and Burmese Muslims - and the role of Muslims in the national movement from the 1920 Rangoon University boycott to the independence struggle and the AFPFL, with lists of Muslim leaders.

သမိုင်းသုတေသီ ဦးမောင်မောင်ကြီး (မန်း) ရေးသားသော မြန်မာပြည်သား မွတ်စလင်များ၏ သမိုင်းနှင့် အမျိုးသားရေးဆိုင်ရာ ပါဝင်မှုအကြောင်း စာအုပ်ဖြစ်သည်။ မြန်မာနိုင်ငံသို့ အစ္စလာမ်သာသနာ ရောက်ရှိလာပုံ၊ ရိုဟင်ဂျာ၊ ကမန်၊ ပန်းသေး၊ ပသျှူးနှင့် မြန်မာမွတ်စလင်စသည့် တိုင်းရင်းသား မွတ်စလင်မျိုးနွယ်စုများနှင့် ၁၉၂၀ ပြည့် ရန်ကုန်တက္ကသိုလ်သပိတ်မှ လွတ်လပ်ရေးတိုက်ပွဲနှင့် ဖဆပလခေတ်အထိ အမျိုးသားလှုပ်ရှားမှုတွင် မွတ်စလင်များ ပါဝင်ခဲ့ပုံကို ဖော်ပြထားပြီး မွတ်စလင်ခေါင်းဆောင်များ၏ အမည်စာရင်းများလည်း ပါဝင်သည်။

A Burmese MA thesis in history by Khin Myat Thway, submitted to the History Department of Yangon University in May 1998. It studies the Japanese occupation of Burma and the anti-fascist resistance in Arakan from 1942 to 1945. edit.mDescription:
A Burmese report compiled by U Aung Win of Sittwe on the 2012 violence between Rakhine and Rohingya in Rakhine State. It gives his account of the causes, including election disputes involving the RNDP party, the Kyauk Ni Maw case of May 2012 and the June 2012 killings, then describes incidents in Sittwe, Maungdaw, Kyauktaw and other towns - killings, burned homes and mosques, looting - with names and places. It ends with short and long-term recommendations on citizenship, movement, education and resettlement.

၂၀၁၂ ခုနှစ် ရခိုင်ပြည်နယ်တွင် ဖြစ်ပွားခဲ့သော ရခိုင်-ရိုဟင်ဂျာ အဓိကရုဏ်းဖြစ်စဉ်များအကြောင်း စစ်တွေမြို့မှ ဦးအောင်ဝင်း စီစဉ်ပြုစုတင်ပြသော အစီရင်ခံစာ ဖြစ်သည်။ RNDP ပါတီပါဝင်သော ရွေးကောက်ပွဲအငြင်းပွားမှုများ၊ ၂၀၁၂ မေလ ကျောက်နီမော်ဖြစ်စဉ်နှင့် ဇွန်လ လူသတ်မှုများ အပါအဝင် အကြောင်းရင်းများကို စာရေးသူ၏ အမြင်ဖြင့် ဖော်ပြပြီး စစ်တွေ၊ မောင်တော၊ ကျောက်တော်နှင့် အခြားမြို့များတွင် ဖြစ်ပွားခဲ့သော လူသတ်မှု၊ နေအိမ်နှင့် ဗလီများ မီးရှို့ခံရမှု၊ လုယက်မှုများကို အမည်များ၊ နေရာများနှင့်တကွ မှတ်တမ်းတင်ထားသည်။ နောက်ဆုံးတွင် နိုင်ငံသားဖြစ်မှု၊ သွားလာခွင့်၊ ပညာရေးနှင့် ပြန်လည်နေရာချထားရေးဆိုင်ရာ ရေတိုနှင့် ရေရှည် အကြံပြုချက်များ ပါဝင်သည်။

Citing Forchhammer, Phayre, Harvey, Pamela Gutman, Jacques Leider and Arakanese chronicles, he discusses Arakan's early Indian kingdoms, the Chandra dynasty, Muslim influence at Mrauk-U and the meaning of names such as Rohang. The author argues that the Rohingya are an indigenous people of Arakan and calls for history based on evidence.

အဘူအာနင် ရေးသား၍ ၂၀၀၄ ခုနှစ် မေလ ၂၇ ရက်နေ့တွင် ဘန်ကောက်မြို့၌ ပြုစုသော ဆောင်းပါးဖြစ်ပြီး ၂၀၀၂ ခုနှစ်တွင် ဂျပန်၌ ထုတ်ဝေသော စာစောင်အပါအဝင် ရိုဟင်ဂျာသမိုင်းကို ငြင်းပယ်ဝေဖန်ရေးသားနေသူများကို တုံ့ပြန်ထားသည်။ ဖော့ခ်ဟမ်မာ၊ ဖေယာ၊ ဟာဗေး၊ ပါမဲလာ ဂပ်မင်၊ ဂျက်ခ်လိုက်ဒါနှင့် ရခိုင်ရာဇဝင်များကို ကိုးကား၍ ရခိုင်ဒေသ၏ ရှေးဟောင်းအိန္ဒိယနိုင်ငံများ၊ စန္ဒြမင်းဆက်၊ မြောက်ဦးခေတ် မွတ်စလင်လွှမ်းမိုးမှုနှင့် ရိုဟန်ကဲ့သို့ အမည်များ၏ အဓိပ္ပာယ်ကို ဆွေးနွေးထားသည်။ စာရေးသူက ရိုဟင်ဂျာများသည် ရခိုင်ဒေသ၏ တိုင်းရင်းသားများ ဖြစ်သည်ဟု ဆိုကာ အထောက်အထားအပေါ် အခြေခံသော သမိုင်းကို တောင်းဆိုထားသည်။
Author        : Abu Anin
Year          : 2004

edit.title: Arakan-Coin
edit.mDescription:
An illustrated Burmese study of old Arakanese coins, compiled from posts on the Ancient Myanmar blog. It argues that a British Museum coin read as King Niti Chandra's is wrongly identified, shows Vesali-period Chandra coins with bull and srivatsa symbols, and lists Mrauk-U kings from the 15th to 18th centuries with photos of their coins, many bearing Arabic or Persian script beside Arakanese. Pyu and Funan coins are shown for comparison, with sources such as The Coin Atlas.

ရှေးဟောင်းရခိုင်ဒင်္ဂါးများအကြောင်း ရုပ်ပုံများဖြင့် မြန်မာဘာသာဖြင့် လေ့လာထားသော စာတမ်းဖြစ်ပြီး Ancient Myanmar ဘလော့ဂ်ပါ ဆောင်းပါးများမှ စုစည်းထားသည်။ ဗြိတိသျှပြတိုက်ရှိ နိတိစန္ဒ ဒင်္ဂါးဟု သတ်မှတ်ထားသော ဒင်္ဂါးသည် မှားယွင်းနေကြောင်း ဆိုထားပြီး နွားနှင့် သိရိဝစ္ဆ သင်္ကေတပါ ဝေသာလီခေတ် စန္ဒြဒင်္ဂါးများ၊ ၁၅ မှ ၁၈ ရာစုအတွင်း မြောက်ဦးဘုရင်များ၏ စာရင်းနှင့် ရခိုင်စာနှင့်အတူ အာရဗီ သို့မဟုတ် ပါရှန်းစာပါသော ၎င်းတို့၏ ဒင်္ဂါးဓာတ်ပုံများကို ဖော်ပြထားသည်။ နှိုင်းယှဉ်ရန် ပျူနှင့် ဖူနန်ဒင်္ဂါးများကိုလည်း ပြထားပြီး The Coin Atlas ကဲ့သို့ ရင်းမြစ်များကို ကိုးကားထားသည်။
Language      : Burmese
Pages         : 21
File Size     : 0.7 MB

edit.title: King Bahadu-Shah
edit.mDescription:
A short Burmese account of the last days of Bahadur Shah Zafar, the last Mughal emperor, who was exiled by the British to Rangoon and died there in 1862. Drawing on Myat Shwe Kalaung's book on the emperor, it covers his youth and Sufi training, his life as a poet in the Delhi palace under British pensions, diary records from 1857 to 1858, his last words, and his first days in exile. Some of his Urdu verse is quoted.

ဗြိတိသျှတို့က ရန်ကုန်မြို့သို့ ပြည်နှင်ခဲ့ပြီး ၁၈၆၂ ခုနှစ်တွင် ထိုမြို့၌ ကွယ်လွန်ခဲ့သော နောက်ဆုံး မဂိုဘုရင် ဘဟာဒူးရှား ဇဖါရ်၏ နောက်ဆုံးနေ့များအကြောင်း မြန်မာဘာသာဖြင့် အကျဉ်းရေးသားထားခြင်း ဖြစ်သည်။ စာရေးဆရာ မြတ်ရွှေကလောင်၏ ဘုရင်ကြီးအကြောင်း စာအုပ်ကို ကိုးကား၍ ငယ်စဉ်ဘဝနှင့် ဆူဖီလမ်းစဉ်လေ့လာမှု၊ ဗြိတိသျှ ငွေကြေးထောက်ပံ့မှုအောက်ရှိ ဒေလီနန်းတော်တွင် ကဗျာဆရာအဖြစ် နေထိုင်ခဲ့ပုံ၊ ၁၈၅၇ မှ ၁၈၅၈ အထိ နေ့စဉ်မှတ်တမ်းများ၊ နောက်ဆုံးစကားများနှင့် ပြည်နှင်ဒဏ်ခံရစဉ် ပထမဆုံးနေ့များကို ဖော်ပြထားသည်။ ဘုရင်၏ အူရဒူကဗျာအချို့ကိုလည်း ကိုးကားထားသည်။
Language      : Burmese
Pages         : 12
File Size     : 0.0 MB

edit.title: King List of Arakan Kingdom
edit.mDescription:
A Burmese king list of Arakan compiled by the monk Ashin Dhammawuntha (Nay La Sekya) of Mrauk-U, based on Arakanese chronicles and on Tun Shwe Khaing's prize-winning dynastic history. In tables it gives each king's name, years of accession and reign and his queen, period by period - the three Dhanyawadi periods, Vesali, Lemro cities such as Pyinsa, Parein, Hkrit and Launggyet, and the Mrauk-U kings to 1784 - with a summary of the dynasties and how long each lasted.

မြောက်ဦးမြို့မှ နေလစကြာ အရှင်ဓမ္မဝံသ ပြုစုသော ရခိုင်ဘုရင်များ၏ စာရင်းဖြစ်ပြီး ရခိုင်ရာဇဝင်များနှင့် ဆုရ ဆရာထွန်းရွှေခိုင်၏ နန်းဆက်မင်းဆက် ရာဇဝင်ကို အခြေခံထားသည်။ ဓညဝတီခေတ် သုံးခေတ်၊ ဝေသာလီခေတ်၊ ပဉ္စာ၊ ပရိန်၊ ခရိတ်၊ လောင်းကြက်စသည့် လေးမြို့ခေတ်နှင့် ၁၇၈၄ ခုနှစ်အထိ မြောက်ဦးခေတ် ဘုရင်များ၏ အမည်၊ နန်းတက်နှစ်၊ နန်းစံနှစ်နှင့် မိဖုရားတို့ကို ဇယားများဖြင့် ဖော်ပြထားပြီး ခေတ်အလိုက် မင်းဆက်များနှင့် နှစ်ပေါင်းကို အကျဉ်းချုပ်ထားသည်။
Author        : Ashin Dhammawuntha (Nay La Sekya)
Language      : Burmese
Pages         : 14
File Size     : 7.9 MB

edit.title: Northern Arakan District
edit.mDescription:
A volume of the colonial Burma Gazetteer on the Northern Arakan District, or Arakan Hill Tracts (today's Paletwa area of Chin State), compiled by the British official G. E. R. Grant Brown and reprinted in Rangoon in 1960. It describes the land, rivers and climate, history and archaeology, the hill peoples such as the Khami, Mro, Chin and Shandu and their customs, farming, forests, trade, administration, police, education and health, and ends with a list of officers since 1887, an index and a map.
Author        : G.E.R. Grant Brown
Year          : 1960
Language      : English
Publisher     : Superintendent, Government Printing and Stationery, Union of Burma, Rangoon
Pages         : 39
File Size     : 13.2 MB

edit.title: The Rohingyas
edit.mDescription:
'The Rohingyas - A Short Account of Their History and Culture' by the Bangladeshi historian Dr. Abdul Karim, first published by the Arakan Historical Society in Chittagong in June 2000. Its six chapters cover the ancient cities of Arakan, the coming of Muslims and the Arakanese kings with Muslim names, Muslim ministers and officers at the Mrauk-U court, Muslim poets of Arakan who wrote in Bengali, and the Rohingya Muslims of Arakan, with maps, a bibliography and a note on the author.
Author        : Dr. Abdul Karim
Year          : 2000
Language      : English
Publisher     : Arakan Historical Society, Chittagong
Pages         : 134
File Size     : 2.8 MB

edit.title: Arakan (Rakhine State): A Land in Conflict on Myanmar's Western Frontier
edit.mDescription:
A detailed history and political study of Arakan by Martin Smith, published by the Transnational Institute in Amsterdam in December 2019. It moves from the Arakan kingdom and British rule through the parliamentary era, Ne Win's rule, the SLORC-SPDC years and the Thein Sein government to the NLD period. Topics include the 2012 violence, Rakhine nationalism, armed groups such as the Arakan Army and ARSA, the Rohingya exodus and China's role, ending with a Rohingya postscript and conclusions.
Author        : Martin Smith
Year          : 2019
Language      : English
Publisher     : Transnational Institute (TNI), Amsterdam
Pages         : 160
File Size     : 7.9 MB

edit.title: The Rohingyas of Arakan: Their Quest for Justice
edit.mDescription:
A long history of the Rohingya written from a Rohingya point of view by A. F. K. Jilani, first published in December 1999, with a foreword by Edith Mirante. Its 42 chapters run from Arakan's geography, the Mrauk-U empire and Shah Shuja through British rule and independence to the Mayu Frontier Administration, citizenship law, Rohingya armed and political groups such as the RIF, RPF, RSO and ARNO, and the refugee crises of the 1990s. Appendices include Brigadier Aung Gyi's 1961 speech.
Author        : A.F.K. Jilani
Year          : 1999
Language      : English
Publisher     : Ahmed Jilani
Pages         : 457
File Size     : 11.0 MB

edit.title: Rohingyas: Tears Down the Cheeks
edit.mDescription:
A collection of about 27 articles by the Rohingya writer Ahmedur Rahman Farooq, published in news media and gathered in Norway in November 2009, with forewords by Shwe Lu Maung and Habib Siddiqui. The articles cover persecution and abuses against the Rohingya in Arakan, Rohingya boat people and refugees in Bangladesh and Thailand, Burma's 2008 constitution and military rule, the 8888 and Saffron uprisings, Rohingya culture and population, and how world media report on the Rohingya.
Author        : Ahmedur Rahman Farooq
Year          : 2009
Language      : English
Pages         : 126
File Size     : 3.4 MB

edit.title: Irrefutable Rohingya: State's Denial in Way to Genocide
edit.mDescription:
A book by Aung Aung of Sittwe, dated December 2016, on the history of Arakan and the rights of the Rohingya. The first part covers the background history of Arakan, its language, and Buddhism and Islam there, and the author argues that the original people of Arakan were Indo-Aryan rather than Rakhine. The second part covers Rohingya heritage and language, Muslims at the royal courts of Mrauk-U, the 1982 Citizenship Law, the 1942 and 2012 violence and the Rakhine Commission, and the author argues that state policy is leading to genocide.
Author        : Aung Aung
Year          : 2016
Language      : English
Pages         : 206
File Size     : 5.3 MB

edit.title: مےیو کا مستقبل (The Future of Mayu), Part 1
edit.mDescription:
A Burmese government booklet in Urdu with the speech of Colonel Aung Gyi, deputy chief of the Burmese army, at the surrender of Mujahid fighters in Maungdaw on 4 July 1961, when more than 290 fighters handed in their weapons. In the speech he describes the Muslims living east of the Pakistan border as Rohingya, asks Rohingya leaders and religious scholars to work with the new Mayu Frontier Administration, and promises peace and development. It has a map of the Mayu area and photos of Aung Gyi and Lt. Col. Ye Gaung.
Author        : Colonel Aung Gyi
Language      : Urdu
Pages         : 23
File Size     : 1.7 MB

edit.title: သိန်းစိန်ထံရိုဟင်ဂျာတွေရဲ့အိတ်ဖွင့်ပေးစာ
edit.mDescription:
An open letter in Burmese to President Thein Sein, dated 12 December 2012 and signed by Kyaw Soe Aung of Yangon, with copies to three ministries and all political parties. The writer argues that Muslims in Arakan have called themselves Rohingya for centuries, not only since independence. He cites Francis Buchanan's 18th-century word list, the Muslim titles of the Mrauk-U kings and the two Rohingya members of the 1947 constitution committee, and asks that the Rohingya be recognised as an indigenous people.

Author        : Kyaw Soe Aung
Year          : 2012
Language      : Burmese
File Size     : 0.04 MB

edit.title: Rohingya being the Indigenous
edit.mDescription:
An unsigned six-page paper in English titled "An assessment of the question of Rohingya's Nationality", on the legal ties between the Rohingya and the Burmese state. The writer argues that the Rohingya are not foreigners and lists the grounds, such as colonial census practice, foreigner registration laws, Rohingya members of the 1947 Constituent Assembly, National Registration Cards issued from 1954, passports, and the right to vote and stand in elections up to 2010. It includes a list of Rohingya MPs from 1936 to 1956 and quotes UNHCR on movement restrictions in northern Rakhine.
Language      : English
Pages         : 6
File Size     : 1.3 MB

edit.title: Rohingya MPs letter to burma human rights commission
edit.mDescription:
A letter in Burmese dated 10 February 2012 from two Rohingya members of the lower house of parliament, U Aung Zaw Win (Maungdaw) and U Shwe Maung (Buthidaung), to the chairman of its Citizens' Fundamental Rights, Democracy and Human Rights Committee. It deals with the Rohingya and the 1982 Citizenship Law. The MPs list evidence that earlier governments treated the Rohingya as an indigenous people, such as a 1959 speech by Prime Minister U Ba Swe, Rohingya-language radio broadcasts in the 1960s, army journal articles and Brigadier Aung Gyi's 1961 speech, and ask that Rohingya be given full citizenship cards.

၂၀၁၂ ခုနှစ် ဖေဖော်ဝါရီ ၁၀ ရက်စွဲဖြင့် ရိုဟင်ဂျာ ပြည်သူ့လွှတ်တော်ကိုယ်စားလှယ် နှစ်ဦးဖြစ်သော ဦးအောင်ဇော်ဝင်း (မောင်တော) နှင့် ဦးရွှေမောင် (ဘူးသီးတောင်) တို့က ပြည်သူ့လွှတ်တော် နိုင်ငံသားများ၏ မူလအခွင့်အရေး၊ ဒီမိုကရေစီရေးနှင့် လူ့အခွင့်အရေးကော်မတီ ဥက္ကဋ္ဌထံ ပေးပို့သော စာ ဖြစ်သည်။ ရိုဟင်ဂျာလူမျိုးများနှင့် ၁၉၈၂ ခုနှစ် မြန်မာနိုင်ငံသားဥပဒေအကြောင်း ဖြစ်သည်။ ၁၉၅၉ ခုနှစ် ဝန်ကြီးချုပ် ဦးဘဆွေ၏ မိန့်ခွန်း၊ ၁၉၆၀ ပြည့်နှစ်များက ရိုဟင်ဂျာဘာသာ အသံလွှင့်အစီအစဉ်၊ တပ်မတော်စာစောင်ပါ ဆောင်းပါးများနှင့် ဗိုလ်မှူးချုပ်အောင်ကြီး၏ ၁၉၆၁ ခုနှစ် မိန့်ခွန်း စသည်တို့ကို ကိုးကားကာ ယခင်အစိုးရများက ရိုဟင်ဂျာများကို တိုင်းရင်းသားအဖြစ် သတ်မှတ်ခဲ့ကြောင်း တင်ပြပြီး နိုင်ငံသားစိစစ်ရေးကတ်ပြား (ပန်းရောင်) ထုတ်ပေးရန် တောင်းဆိုထားသည်။
Author        : U Aung Zaw Win and U Shwe Maung
Year          : 2012
Language      : Burmese
Pages         : 5

edit.title: နစကတပ်စခန်းများ
edit.mDescription:
A three-page table in Burmese listing the camps of the NaSaKa, the border security force that operated in northern Rakhine State until 2013. It gives the headquarters of its nine sectors and about 70 camps and outposts under them, with the village where each one stood in Maungdaw, Buthidaung and Rathedaung townships, often with the Rohingya name of the village in brackets.

ရခိုင်ပြည်နယ်မြောက်ပိုင်းတွင် ၂၀၁၃ ခုနှစ်အထိ တာဝန်ထမ်းဆောင်ခဲ့သော နယ်စပ်လုံခြုံရေးတပ်ဖွဲ့ နစကတပ်၏ စခန်းများကို စာရင်းပြုစုထားသော မြန်မာဘာသာ ဇယား သုံးမျက်နှာ ဖြစ်သည်။ နယ်မြေ ကိုးခု၏ နယ်မြေမှူးရုံးများနှင့် ၎င်းတို့အောက်ရှိ စခန်းနှင့် ကင်းစခန်း ၇၀ ခန့်ကို မောင်တော၊ ဘူးသီးတောင်နှင့် ရသေ့တောင် မြို့နယ်များရှိ တည်ရှိရာ ကျေးရွာအမည်များနှင့်တကွ ဖော်ပြထားပြီး ရွာအများစု၏ ရိုဟင်ဂျာအမည်ကို ကွင်းစကွင်းပိတ်ဖြင့် ထည့်ပေးထားသည်။

edit.title: Rohingya: Indigenous, Ethnic Cleansing
edit.mDescription:
Presentation slides by Dr. Hla Kyaw of the European Rohingya Council, given at the Varbergs Peace Forum in Sweden on 23 October 2015. They present the Rohingya as an indigenous people once recognised by Burmese governments, with quotes from U Ba Swe and Sao Shwe Thaik and Rohingya MPs from 1936 to 2010. They then list operations against the Rohingya from 1965, the 1982 Citizenship Law, the 2012 violence, the IDP camps and the race and religion laws, and end with calls to the UN, the EU and activists.
Author        : Dr. Hla Kyaw
Year          : 2015
Language      : English
Pages         : 31
File Size     : 8.2 MB

edit.mDescription:
The official British gazetteer of Akyab District, the area around Sittwe, Maungdaw, Buthidaung and Mrauk-U, compiled by R. B. Smart and completed in 1917. Its chapters cover geography and climate, the history of the Arakan kings, the Portuguese and the First Anglo-Burmese War, the old towns and pagodas, the peoples and their customs and migration, farming, forests, trade, transport, administration, land revenue, schools and public health. edit.mDescription:
The statistical volume (Volume B, No. 3) of the British Burma Gazetteer for Kyaukpyu District on the Arakan coast, with its townships of Kyaukpyu, An, Ramree, Cheduba and Myebon, printed in Rangoon in 1924. Part I gives general facts such as administrative divisions, towns, urban population by religion, roads, ferries, wages and police. Part II has tables from annual returns on rainfall, vital statistics, farming, forests, trade, revenue and crime. Part III lists the towns and villages with their population from the 1921 census.
Author        : Government of Burma

edit.mDescription:
The British district gazetteer of Sandoway (Thandwe) in southern Arakan, written by Deputy Commissioner W. B. Tydd with figures up to the 1911 census. Its chapters describe the land, rivers and climate, the history from the Arakan kingdom through the Burmese conquest and the Anglo-Burmese wars, the peoples (Arakanese, Burmans, Chins, Muslims and Indians) and their languages and religions, farming, forests, trades, roads, administration, revenue, schools and public health, with short notes on Sandoway, Taungup and Gwa townships.

edit.mDescription:

Part I gives general facts such as area, administrative divisions, district staff, police, towns, ferries, fisheries, roads, population by race and language, migration, literacy and wages. Part II has statistical tables on rainfall, population, farming, crops, forests, trade, revenue and other subjects, and the volume ends with town and village census tables.

edit.title: History of Arakan (Handwritten, 1982)
edit.mDescription:
A hand-lettered history of Arakan in Rohingya, written in the Hanifi script, with the English title "A History of Arakan" on a cover showing old Arakanese coins with Arabic inscriptions. It contains maps, tables of the kings of Arakan with their dates, a part on the Muslims of Arakan with English references to historians such as Hall, Harvey and Collis, and photos of mosques and of R.S.O. leaders. It ends with a timeline of events from 1942 to the violence of May and June 2012.

edit.title: History of Arakan (Rohingya)
edit.mDescription:
A short hand-lettered history of Arakan in Rohingya, written in the Hanifi script, with numbered pages in decorative frames. It opens with a map of Arakan, and its brief chapters are illustrated with portraits of people from Rohingya history and a drawing of an old sailing ship. The opening page names an Urdu work, Tarikh-e-Arakan (History of Arakan), and the back cover carries an emblem marked R.E.B.M.

edit.title: History of the Rohingya (Handwritten, 1989)
edit.mDescription:
A hand-lettered booklet in Rohingya, written in the Hanifi script and dated 1989 on its title page. It opens with a page of dated entries from the 8th century onward. The rest is short illustrated lessons, mostly question-and-answer dialogues and readings, with drawings of two men talking, a doctor with a patient, a boy and a girl, a telephone call and a handshake. It looks like a reader for learning Rohingya more than a history book.
Year          : 1989
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 20
File Size     : 7.2 MB

edit.title: Memoir of Mrs. Sarah D. Comstock, Missionary to Arracan
edit.mDescription:
A memoir of Sarah Davis Comstock, an American Baptist missionary in Arakan, written by Amanda M. Edmond and published in Philadelphia in 1854. Built largely from her letters and journals, it follows her early religious life in Massachusetts, the voyage to Burma, mission work at Kyaukpyu and later Ramree, her remarks on the manners and habits of the Arakanese, illness among the missionaries, the sending of her children back to America, and her last days.
Author        : Amanda M. Edmond
Year          : 1854
Language      : English
Publisher     : American Baptist Publication Society, Philadelphia
Pages         : 242
File Size     : 5.7 MB

edit.title: Narrative of the Shipwreck of the Juno on the Coast of Aracan
edit.mDescription:
An account by William Mackay, second mate of the Juno, written as a letter to his father and printed in London in 1798. The ship, carrying teak from Rangoon to Madras, was wrecked in 1795 and lay half-sunk off the coast of Arakan, where only fourteen of its people survived. He describes their weeks on the wreck, reaching the shore, their treatment by local people and a zamindar near Ramu and Chittagong, and his later return to the wreck. Footnotes describe Rangoon and the teak trade.
Author        : William Mackay
Year          : 1798
Language      : English
Publisher     : J. Debrett, London
Pages         : 75
File Size     : 10.6 MB

edit.title: Notes on Arakan
edit.mDescription:
A long article by the late Rev. G. S. Comstock, an American Baptist missionary in Arakan from 1834 to 1844, published in the Journal of the American Oriental Society with a map by his colleague L. Stilson and notes by the editor. It describes the land and its peoples with population figures for Arakanese, Burmese, Muslims, Chins and others, then farming and trade, religions, education, family life, houses, dress and food, and British rule in Arakan.
Author        : G. S. Comstock
Year          : 1847
Language      : English
Publisher     : American Oriental Society (Journal, Vol. I, No. III)
Pages         : 48
File Size     : 8.6 MB

edit.title: Report on the Administration of the Hill Tracts, Northern Arakan, 1871–72
edit.mDescription:
The first yearly report on the new Hill Tracts district of northern Arakan under British rule, written by its Superintendent, Captain W. G. Hughes, in June 1872 and printed in Rangoon with the Chief Commissioner's response. It covers raids by the Shendu and other tribes beyond the frontier, captives and slavery, the police, trade and a new bazaar at Daletme, revenue, and the customs and languages of the hill peoples such as the Chins, with proposals for governing them.
Author        : Captain W. G. Hughes
Year          : 1872
Language      : English
Publisher     : Secretariat Press, Rangoon
Pages         : 76
File Size     : 51.2 MB

edit.title: Rohingya History: Myth and Reality
edit.mDescription:
A short book by Zul Nurain, published as a free e-book by Ovi Project Books in 2010, that answers critics of Rohingya history writing, especially a critique published in Japan in 2003. The author argues that Rakhine historians have hidden the Muslim part of Arakan's past. He discusses the early settlers of Arakan, the Wesali period, Muslim links of the Mrauk-U kings, the murder of Shah Shuja, British rule, and Rohingya nationality, and replies point by point to claims that the Rohingya are recent migrants.
Author        : Zul Nurain (U Kyaw Min)
Year          : 2010
Language      : English
Publisher     : Ovi Project Books (Chameleon Project)
Pages         : 76
File Size     : 0.5 MB

edit.title: The Arakan Operations, 1942–45
edit.mDescription:
A volume of the Official History of the Indian Armed Forces in the Second World War, describing the fighting in Arakan between British, Indian and African troops and the Japanese from late 1942 to the end of the war. Its 21 chapters open with the land and its people, then follow the first Arakan offensive, the Japanese counter-attacks of 1943 and 1944, the monsoon periods, and the 1945 operations at Myebon and Kangaw and the landings on Ramree and Akyab, with 25 maps and appendices.
Author        : Lt.-Col. N. N. Madan
Editor        : Bisheshwar Prasad
Year          : 1954
Language      : English

edit.title: The Burmese & Arakanese Calendars
edit.mDescription:
A study of the Burmese and Arakanese lunisolar calendars by A. M. B. Irwin of the Indian Civil Service, printed in Rangoon in 1909 as an enlarged version of his 1901 book on the Burmese calendar. It explains the Hindu astronomical sources of the calendars, the Burmese terms for days, months and years, how the calendars are calculated, their errors and proposed reforms. Long tables let readers convert English dates to Burmese dates and back for the years 1739 to 2000.
Author        : A. M. B. Irwin
Year          : 1909
Language      : English

edit.title: Travels of Fray Sebastien Manrique, 1629–1643
edit.mDescription:
The first volume, titled Arakan, of the English translation of the travels of Sebastien Manrique, a Portuguese Augustinian friar, first issued by the Hakluyt Society in 1927. After an introduction on his life and routes, he describes Bengal and its people, then his journeys to the Arakan court at Mrauk-U, the city and its customs and festivals, the coronation of King Thiri Thudhamma, Christian missions in Arakan and Chittagong, and his shipwreck and imprisonment. It ends with his travels on to India and Ceylon.
Author        : Sebastien Manrique
Translator    : C. Eckford Luard, assisted by H. Hosten
Year          : 2016
Language      : English

Pages         : 478
File Size     : 6.8 MB

edit.title: The History of India as Told by Its Own Historians, Vol. I
edit.mDescription:
The first volume of a classic collection of English translations from Arabic and Persian sources on India, prepared from the papers of Sir H. M. Elliot and edited by John Dowson in 1867. It gives extracts from early Arab geographers such as the merchant Sulaiman, Mas'udi, Ibn Haukal, al-Idrisi and al-Biruni, and from histories of Sind such as the Chach-nama. An appendix note on the kingdom of Rahma, described by the Arab geographers, suggests it lay on the Bay of Bengal near Dacca and Arakan.

An official history of Kyaukphyu Township in Rakhine State, compiled from August 1981 by committees of the Township People's Council on the orders of the Rakhine State People's Council and dated 10 May 1982. It covers the founding of the town, its famous pagodas, British rule, geography, climate and population, then political history from colonial times through the parliamentary and socialist eras, the local economy, education, health, culture, sports, religion and literature.

ရခိုင်ပြည်နယ် ပြည်သူ့ကောင်စီ၏ ညွှန်ကြားချက်အရ ကျောက်ဖြူမြို့နယ် ပြည်သူ့ကောင်စီမှ ကော်မတီများ ဖွဲ့စည်းကာ ၁၉၈၁ ခုနှစ် ဩဂုတ်လမှ စတင် ပြုစုခဲ့ပြီး ၁၉၈၂ ခုနှစ် မေလ ၁၀ ရက်စွဲပါသော ကျောက်ဖြူမြို့နယ် ဖြစ်စဉ်သမိုင်း မှတ်တမ်း ဖြစ်သည်။ မြို့စတင်တည်ထောင်ခြင်း၊ ထင်ရှားသော ဘုရားပုထိုးများ၊ ဗြိတိသျှခေတ်၊ ပထဝီဝင်၊ ရာသီဥတုနှင့် လူဦးရေ၊ ကိုလိုနီခေတ်မှ ပါလီမန်ဒီမိုကရေစီခေတ်နှင့် ဆိုရှယ်လစ်ခေတ်အထိ နိုင်ငံရေးဖြစ်စဉ်၊ စီးပွားရေး၊ ပညာရေး၊ ကျန်းမာရေး၊ ယဉ်ကျေးမှု၊ အားကစား၊ ဘာသာရေးနှင့် စာပေတို့ကို ဖော်ပြထားသည်။
Author        : Kyaukphyu Township People's Council
Year          : 1982

edit.title: ဘူးသီးတောင်မြို့နယ် ဖြစ်စဉ်သမိုင်း
edit.mDescription:
An official history of Buthidaung Township in northern Rakhine State, compiled in the mid-1990s under the military government, with no compiler named. Its 15 chapters cover geography, history, peoples and religions, the economy, forests, industry, transport, administration, taxes, development work, education and health, with appendices of villages, ethnic groups and monasteries in 1994. A chapter titled "Bengalis who call themselves Rohingya" argues that the township's Muslim majority are Bengalis and that the name Rohingya has no historical basis, and appendices list what it calls Bengali villages.

ရခိုင်ပြည်နယ်မြောက်ပိုင်း ဘူးသီးတောင်မြို့နယ်၏ ဖြစ်စဉ်သမိုင်းကို စစ်အစိုးရလက်ထက် ၁၉၉၀ ပြည့်လွန်နှစ်များ အလယ်ပိုင်းခန့်တွင် ပြုစုထားခြင်းဖြစ်ပြီး ပြုစုသူအမည် မပါရှိပါ။ အခန်း ၁၅ ခန်းတွင် ပထဝီဝင်၊ သမိုင်း၊ လူမျိုးများနှင့် ကိုးကွယ်ယုံကြည်မှု၊ စီးပွားရေး၊ သစ်တော၊ စက်မှု၊ ပို့ဆောင်ဆက်သွယ်ရေး၊ အုပ်ချုပ်ရေး၊ အခွန်ကောက်ခံရေး၊ ဖွံ့ဖြိုးရေးလုပ်ငန်းများ၊ ပညာရေးနှင့် ကျန်းမာရေးတို့ကို ဖော်ပြထားပြီး ၁၉၉၄ ခုနှစ်က ကျေးရွာများ၊ လူမျိုးများနှင့် ကျောင်းများစာရင်းကို နောက်ဆက်တွဲအဖြစ် ထည့်သွင်းထားသည်။ "ရိုဟင်ဂျာအမည်ခံ ဘင်္ဂါလီလူမျိုးများ" ဟူသော အခန်းတွင် မြို့နယ်ရှိ မွတ်စလင်အများစုသည် ဘင်္ဂါလီများဖြစ်ပြီး ရိုဟင်ဂျာဟူသော အမည်မှာ သမိုင်းအခြေခံ မရှိဟု စာရေးသူက ဆိုထားကာ ဘင်္ဂါလီကျေးရွာများဟု ၎င်းခေါ်ဆိုသော ရွာစာရင်းများကိုလည်း ထည့်သွင်းထားသည်။

A history of Minbya Township in Rakhine State, compiled by a committee of scholars and officials set up by the Township People's Council, with figures up to 1981-82. It opens with a poem on the town's origins, then covers geography, population, religions and ethnic groups, the founding of the town and its pagodas. Later parts cover the feudal, British, Japanese, parliamentary and socialist periods, then education, health, sports, farming, fishing, forests, industry, trade, transport, culture, literature and local proverbs.

edit.title: မြောက်ဦးမြို့နယ် ဖြစ်စဉ်သမိုင်း
edit.mDescription:
An official record of Mrauk-U Township in Rakhine State, compiled from June to August 1982 by a township committee under the guidance of the ruling Burma Socialist Programme Party. It covers geography, climate and wildlife, then a long history from the Wesali period with lists of the kings of the Wesali, Launggyet and Mrauk-U dynasties and their reigns, followed by the anti-colonial and political movements of the township, its culture and literature, local customs, and the names of the committee members.

၁၉၈၂ ခုနှစ် ဇွန်လမှ ဩဂုတ်လအတွင်း မြန်မာ့ဆိုရှယ်လစ်လမ်းစဉ်ပါတီ၏ ဦးဆောင်မှုဖြင့် မြို့နယ်မှတ်တမ်းပြုစုရေးကော်မတီက ပြုစုခဲ့သော ရခိုင်ပြည်နယ် မြောက်ဦးမြို့နယ် ဖြစ်စဉ်သမိုင်း မှတ်တမ်း ဖြစ်သည်။ ပထဝီဝင်၊ ရာသီဥတုနှင့် သားငှက်တိရစ္ဆာန်များ၊ ဝေသာလီခေတ်မှစ၍ ဝေသာလီ၊ လောင်းကြက်နှင့် မြောက်ဦး မင်းဆက်များ၏ နန်းစံနှစ်စာရင်းများပါဝင်သော သမိုင်း၊ မြို့နယ်၏ နယ်ချဲ့ဆန့်ကျင်ရေးနှင့် နိုင်ငံရေးလှုပ်ရှားမှုများ၊ ယဉ်ကျေးမှုနှင့် စာပေ၊ ဒေသဓလေ့ထုံးစံများနှင့် ကော်မတီဝင်များစာရင်းကို ဖော်ပြထားသည်။
Author        : Mrauk-U Township Record Compilation Committee
Year          : 1982
Language      : Burmese
Pages         : 84
File Size     : 0.3 MB

edit.title: သမိုင်းသက်သေ ရိုဟင်ဂျာ (အဖြေ)
edit.mDescription:
A book in Burmese by the translator U Aung Khin of Sittwe, published in August 2012 after the violence in Rakhine State that May and June. The author argues that the Rohingya are an indigenous people of Arakan. He covers the geography of Rakhine and the origin of the name Rohingya, the peoples of the state, the views of historians, Muslims under the Arakanese kings and their coins, Rohingya in the independence movement, Rohingya-language radio broadcasts, population figures, and the constitutions and the 1982 Citizenship Law.

ရခိုင်ပြည်နယ်တွင် ၂၀၁၂ ခုနှစ် မေ၊ ဇွန်လများအတွင်း ဖြစ်ပွားခဲ့သော အဓိကရုဏ်းများအပြီး ၂၀၁၂ ခုနှစ် ဩဂုတ်လတွင် ထုတ်ဝေခဲ့သည့် စစ်တွေမှ ဘာသာပြန်စာရေးဆရာ ဦးအောင်ခင်၏ စာအုပ်ဖြစ်သည်။ ရိုဟင်ဂျာများသည် ရခိုင်ဒေသ၏ ဌာနေတိုင်းရင်းသားများ ဖြစ်ကြောင်း စာရေးသူက ဆိုထားသည်။ ရခိုင်ဒေသ၏ ပထဝီဝင်နှင့် ရိုဟင်ဂျာအမည် ပေါ်ပေါက်လာပုံ၊ ပြည်နယ်ရှိ လူမျိုးများ၊ သမိုင်းဆရာများ၏ အမြင်၊ ရခိုင်ဘုရင်များလက်ထက်က မွတ်စလင်များနှင့် ဒင်္ဂါးများ၊ လွတ်လပ်ရေးလှုပ်ရှားမှုတွင် ရိုဟင်ဂျာများ ပါဝင်ခဲ့ပုံ၊ ရိုဟင်ဂျာဘာသာ အသံလွှင့်အစီအစဉ်၊ လူဦးရေနှင့် ဖွဲ့စည်းပုံအခြေခံဥပဒေများ၊ ၁၉၈၂ ခုနှစ် နိုင်ငံသားဥပဒေတို့ကို ဖော်ပြထားသည်။
Author        : ဦးအောင်ခင် (စစ်တွေ) (U Aung Khin, Sittwe)
Year          : 2012
Language      : Burmese
Publisher     : U Aung Khin, Shwepyitha, Yangon
Pages         : 140
File Size     : 14.7 MB

edit.title: အာရကန်ဌာနေ တိုင်းရင်းသားရိုဟင်ဂျာ
edit.mDescription:
A set of 33 numbered picture cards in Burmese, made for social media and signed Ro Nay San Lwin, under the title "Rohingya, an indigenous people of Arakan". Each card gives one piece of evidence the author offers for that view, such as Francis Buchanan's 1799 record of the name, Rohingya members of parliament and ministers from 1936 to 1990, U Nu's 1954 speech, citizenship cards in the 1950s and Rohingya-language radio from 1961 to 1965. The last cards describe the loss of rights from the 1990s and events since 2012.

လူမှုကွန်ရက်အတွက် ပြုလုပ်ထားပြီး ရိုနေဆန်းလွင် လက်မှတ်ပါသော "အာရကန်ဌာနေ တိုင်းရင်းသား ရိုဟင်ဂျာ" ခေါင်းစဉ်ဖြင့် နံပါတ်စဉ်ပါ မြန်မာဘာသာ ပုံကတ် ၃၃ ခု ဖြစ်သည်။ ကတ်တစ်ခုစီတွင် ထိုအမြင်အတွက် စာရေးသူ တင်ပြသည့် အထောက်အထားတစ်ခုစီ ပါဝင်ပြီး ၁၇၉၉ ခုနှစ် ဖရန်စစ် ဘူကာနန်၏ မှတ်တမ်း၊ ၁၉၃၆ မှ ၁၉၉၀ အထိ ရိုဟင်ဂျာ လွှတ်တော်ကိုယ်စားလှယ်များနှင့် ဝန်ကြီးများ၊ ၁၉၅၄ ခုနှစ် ဦးနု၏ မိန့်ခွန်း၊ ၁၉၅၀ ပြည့်နှစ်များက နိုင်ငံသားကတ်ပြားများနှင့် ၁၉၆၁ မှ ၁၉၆၅ အထိ ရိုဟင်ဂျာဘာသာ အသံလွှင့်ချိန် စသည်တို့ ပါဝင်သည်။ နောက်ဆုံးကတ်များတွင် ၁၉၉၀ ပြည့်နှစ်များမှစ၍ အခွင့်အရေးများ ဆုံးရှုံးလာပုံနှင့် ၂၀၁၂ ခုနှစ်နောက်ပိုင်း ဖြစ်ရပ်များကို ဖော်ပြထားသည်။
Author        : Ro Nay San Lwin (ရိုနေဆန်းလွင်)
Language      : Burmese
Pages         : 33
File Size     : 21.6 MB

edit.title: 𐴀𐴝𐴌𐴑𐴝𐴕𐴡𐴌 𐴃𐴝𐴤𐴌𐴞𐴑𐴡𐴌 𐴇𐴞𐴥𐴏𐴄𐴟𐴌𐴞
edit.mDescription:
A short illustrated booklet in Rohingya, written in the Hanifi script, on the history of Arakan and the Rohingya. It is full of pictures, including a cover with portraits and an old coin, photos of Rohingya leaders and elders, Burmese-language quotation cards from Burmese leaders about the Rohingya, a map, photos of an elderly Islamic scholar from Maungdaw, and a poster of past leaders with the slogan "Stop genocide on Rohingya in Arakan State". The last page carries the emblem of the Rohingya Zuban Committee.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 30
File Size     : 22.1 MB

edit.title: တပ်မတော်ခေတ်ရေးစာစောင်
edit.mDescription:
A special Mayu issue of the Burmese army journal Khit Yay, dated 18 July 1961, covering the surrender of Mujahid fighters at Maungdaw on 4 July 1961 and the new Mayu Frontier Administration. It reports the speech of Brigadier Aung Gyi, deputy army chief, who said that the Rohingya living in the Mayu frontier area are citizens of the Union of Burma, with many photos of the ceremony, the frontier area and its people. A note added later in red highlights this passage and appeals to President Thein Sein.

မောင်တောတွင် ၁၉၆၁ ခုနှစ် ဇူလိုင်လ ၄ ရက်နေ့က မူဂျာဟစ်များ လက်နက်ချခြင်းနှင့် မေယုနယ်ခြားဒေသ အုပ်ချုပ်ရေးအကြောင်း ဖော်ပြထားသော ၁၉၆၁ ခုနှစ် ဇူလိုင်လ ၁၈ ရက်နေ့ထုတ် တပ်မတော် ခေတ်ရေးစာစောင် (အတွဲ ၁၂၊ အမှတ် ၆) မေယု အထူးထုတ် ဖြစ်သည်။ မေယုနယ်ခြားဒေသတွင် နေထိုင်ကြသော ရိုဟင်ဂျာ အမျိုးသားများသည် ပြည်ထောင်စု မြန်မာနိုင်ငံတော်သားများ ဖြစ်ကြသည်ဟု ဒု-ကာချုပ် ဗိုလ်မှူးချုပ်အောင်ကြီး ပြောကြားခဲ့သော မိန့်ခွန်းကို ဖော်ပြထားပြီး အခမ်းအနား၊ နယ်ခြားဒေသနှင့် ဒေသခံများ၏ ဓာတ်ပုံများစွာ ပါဝင်သည်။ နောက်ပိုင်းတွင် အနီရောင်ဖြင့် ထည့်သွင်းထားသော မှတ်ချက်က ထိုစာပိုဒ်ကို မီးမောင်းထိုးပြပြီး သမ္မတ ဦးသိန်းစိန်ထံ တောင်းဆိုထားသည်။
Author        : တပ်မတော်
Year          : 1961
Language      : Burmese
Publisher     : Burma Army (Tatmadaw), Khit Yay journal, Vol. 12, No. 6
Pages         : 22
File Size     : 4.3 MB

edit.title: Vaishali-and-the-indianization-of-arakan
edit.mDescription:
A study by the historian Noel F. Singer of Vaishali (Wethali), the early capital of Arakan, and the Indian influence on its culture, published in New Delhi in 2008. Its chapters cover the background history, the Buddha's legendary visit, the inscriptions of the Dhanyawadi and Vaishali periods and especially the Ananda Chandra inscription, the Chandra dynasties and their coins, the city and its religious beliefs, and the museums at Mrauk-U and the Mahamuni shrine. This file holds only selected pages of the book.
Author        : Noel F Singer
Year          : 2008
Language      : English
Publisher     : A.P.H. Publishing Corporation, New Delhi
ISBN          : 978-81-313-0405-1
Pages         : 37
File Size     : 4.7 MB

edit.title: Sow Lombor(𐴏𐴡𐴤𐴓𐴡𐴔𐴁𐴡𐴌)
edit.mDescription:
A short booklet in Rohingya, written in the Hanifi script, on the six qualities (Sitta Sifat, ستة صفات) taught in the Tablighi Jamaat movement, beginning with the Kalimah. Each quality has a heading in Arabic and is explained in Rohingya under sub-headings, with short Arabic quotations. The back cover carries a hadith in Arabic and the emblem of the Rohingya Zuban Committee.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Publisher     : Rohingya Zuban Committee
Pages         : 10
File Size     : 11.8 MB

edit.title: Islam Dormo aek Class
edit.mDescription:
A Class 1 textbook of Islamic religious studies for young children, written in Rohingya in the Hanifi script and published by the Rohingya Zuban Committee. After a short preface and a contents table, it has 16 brief lessons, most written as simple questions and answers about basic Islamic belief and practice, with the Bismillah and a few other phrases given in Arabic.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Publisher     : Rohingya Zuban Committee
Pages         : 22
File Size     : 5.7 MB

edit.title: Salish Hadis
edit.mDescription:
A collection of forty short hadith (Arba'un Hadith, اربعون حديث) with a Rohingya translation in the Hanifi script. Each saying of the Prophet is printed in Arabic with its source, such as Bukhari, Muslim, Tirmidhi or Mishkat, followed by a one-line Rohingya translation. The topics include intention, purity, prayer, seeking knowledge and supplication. A short preface opens the booklet and a Rohingya poem closes it.
Language      : Arabic and Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Publisher     : Rohingya Zuban Committee
Pages         : 14
File Size     : 4.9 MB

edit.title: Rosul(saw) or Nosob Shorif
edit.mDescription:
A book in Rohingya, written in the Hanifi script, on the noble lineage (nasab) of the Prophet Muhammad. It opens with a family-tree diagram and traces his forefathers and relatives, and later sections discuss his family and his noble character, quoting the Quran in Arabic. The preface lists the Arabic sources used, such as Tafsir al-Jalalayn, Fiqh al-Sirah al-Nabawiyya and Tarikh al-Dawla al-Islamiyya.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 52
File Size     : 8.7 MB

edit.title: Faza el Tablig
edit.mDescription:
A Rohingya translation, in the Hanifi script, of Fazail-e-Tabligh (فضائل تبليغ), Maulana Muhammad Zakariya Kandhlawi's book on the virtues of calling people to Islam and of enjoining good and forbidding wrong, widely read in the Tablighi Jamaat. After the translator's prefaces, the text explains the duty of preaching with Quran verses and hadith quoted in Arabic.
Author        : Muhammad Zakariya Kandhlawi
Year          : 2015
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 50
File Size     : 12.2 MB

edit.title: Jonnot Beggun Ottu Aro Shundor
edit.mDescription:
An illustrated story book for children about Paradise (Jannah), written in Rohingya in the Hanifi script. Its title means that Paradise is more beautiful than anything. Told partly through conversations between children and adults and printed over full-page cartoon pictures, it describes the beauty and joys of Paradise, with short Arabic phrases such as Subhanallah and Alhamdulillah. It carries the emblem of the Rohingya Zuban Committee.
Writer        : Zuban Committee
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 36
File Size     : 4.7 MB

edit.title: Tafsir Al Quran
edit.mDescription:
A short Quran booklet in Arabic and Rohingya, with the Rohingya written in the Hanifi script, made by the Rohingya Zuban Committee. After a preface, it gives Surah Al-Fatiha and the ten short surahs from Al-Fil to An-Nas, one surah per page, with each verse in Arabic followed by its Rohingya meaning and short explanations in brackets. It ends with a closing note in Rohingya.
Writer        : Zuban Committee
Language      : Arabic and Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 16
File Size     : 1.9 MB

edit.title: Talimul Islam
edit.mDescription:
A primer on the basics of Islam in Rohingya, written in the Hanifi script and set out as simple questions and answers. After a preface and a table of contents, it begins with the Kalimas, such as the Kalima Tayyiba and the Kalima Shahada given in Arabic with their meaning, and goes on through short sections on Islamic belief and practice. It suits beginners and young learners.
Author        : Hafez Mohammad omor
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 47
File Size     : 7.9 MB

edit.title: Tabliq Jamaat
edit.mDescription:
An introduction to the Tablighi Jamaat, the worldwide Islamic preaching movement, in Rohingya written in the Hanifi script, translated by Noor Qadar in 2019. Arranged in three parts with a contents table, it covers how the movement began in the Mewat region near Delhi and spread to Asia, Europe, North America and Africa, how its work is done, and the manners of eating and drinking with their Arabic supplications. Some key terms are glossed in English.
Translator    : Noor Qadar
Year          : 2019
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Publisher     : Rohingya Zuban (Arakan Branch)
Pages         : 31
File Size     : 23.2 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Azkar
edit.mDescription:
A pocket book of daily Islamic remembrances (azkar) for Rohingya readers. Each dhikr is printed in Arabic with its hadith source, followed by its meaning and its reward explained in Rohingya in the Hanifi script. It covers the remembrances said after the five daily prayers, the morning and evening azkar such as Ayat al-Kursi and blessings on the Prophet, and ends with Quran verses on the virtue of remembering Allah.
Language      : Arabic and Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 37
File Size     : 22.9 MB

edit.title: The Complete Quran Translation in Rohingya
edit.mDescription:
A translation of the meaning of the Quran into Rohingya, written in the Rohingya Latin script (Rohingyalish). It runs from Surah Al-Baqarah to Surah An-Nas, each surah headed by its name in Arabic and Latin letters, with numbered verses and short explanations in brackets. Only the translation is given, not the Arabic text, and Surah Al-Fatiha is not included. The translation was made around 2008 by Eng. Mohammed Siddique.
Translator    : Mohammed Siddique
Language      : Rohingya (Latin script)
Pages         : 357
File Size     : 8.9 MB

edit.title: مكارم الأخلاق (Makarim al-Akhlaq)
edit.mDescription:
A book on Islamic manners and character by Yasir Rashid, published by Mayu Library in 2025. It has forty short numbered topics, each built on a hadith given in Arabic with its source such as Bukhari, Muslim or Tirmidhi, followed by an explanation in Rohingya in the Hanifi script. The first part covers good character, beginning with the virtue of good manners, the second part warns against bad character such as envy and spying, and a last section gives daily remembrances (adhkar).
Author        : Yasir Rashid
Year          : 2025
Language      : Arabic and Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Publisher     : Mayu Library (مكتبة مايو)
Pages         : 53
File Size     : 3.0 MB

edit.title: Islam Dormo Duyom Class
edit.mDescription:
A Class 2 textbook of Islamic religious studies for children, written in Rohingya in the Hanifi script and published by the Rohingya Zuban Committee. After a short preface, its illustrated lessons start with the Holy Quran and the words said before reciting it, given in Arabic, and go on to topics such as famous mosques and the manners of sleeping with the bedtime supplication in Arabic. It follows the committee's Class 1 book.
Writer        : Zuban Committee
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 40
File Size     : 3.6 MB

edit.title: Rosul Or Naam
edit.mDescription:
An illustrated booklet of 99 names and titles of the Prophet Muhammad, two to a page on numbered round cards. Each name is written large in Arabic, such as Muhammad, Ahmad, Hamid and Mahmud, with its meaning in Rohingya in the Hanifi script, in Urdu and in English, for example Highly Praised or The Most Commendable. The last card is Rasul al-Malahim.
Writer        : Zuban Committee
Language      : Arabic, Rohingya (Hanifi script), Urdu and English
Pages         : 52
File Size     : 4.9 MB

edit.title: About the Prophets (Handwritten, 1999)
edit.mDescription:
A handwritten notebook of Islamic knowledge, titled in Urdu Ma'lumat-e Anbiya-e Kiram (information about the noble prophets), written in 1999 by Mohammad Amin Samila of Rathidaung, Arakan. It is written in Rohingya in the Hanifi script with passages in Urdu. It covers the prophets and the history of the Kaaba, with a numbered list of those who built or rebuilt it from the angels and Adam to King Fahd, numbered lists of names, and notes on the imams of the six major hadith collections.
Author        : Mohammad Amin Samila
Year          : 1999
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script) and Urdu
Pages         : 26
File Size     : 10.7 MB

edit.title: Islam Dormo
edit.mDescription:
A school textbook of Islamic religious studies in Rohingya, hand-lettered in the Hanifi script and scanned from a printed copy. The cover shows the Kaaba and the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah. Inside, it is divided into short numbered lessons of one or two pages on Islamic belief and practice, each with numbered points and some footnotes. The back cover carries the emblem of R.E.B (M), the Rohingya education board that issued it.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Publisher     : R.E.B (M)
Pages         : 42
File Size     : 25.7 MB

edit.title: Islamiyat Book 3
edit.mDescription:
A Class 3 textbook of Islamic religious studies for children, in Rohingya written in the Hanifi script, from the Rohingya Zuban Committee's Islam Dormo school series. Its illustrated lessons teach daily practice with Arabic supplications, Quran verses and hadith, such as the prayers for entering and leaving the toilet, how to make wudu, and the duty of prayer, including the hadith on teaching children to pray from the age of seven. The last pages give numbered hadith in Arabic with Rohingya translations.
Language      : Arabic and Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Publisher     : Rohingya Zuban Committee
Pages         : 22
File Size     : 5.0 MB

edit.title: Kul Musalmanor Zoruri Sobok

edit.mDescription:
A history in Burmese by Aye Chan of the first period of the Mrauk-U kingdom of Arakan, 1430 to 1531. It describes the end of the Launggyet period, King Narameikhla's (Min Saw Mon's) exile at the court of the Bengal sultan and his return, the founding of Mrauk-U, and the politics of the kings who followed, including the Muslim-style titles some of them used and Arakan's dealings with Bengal, the Portuguese and the Mughals. Each chapter has endnotes citing Arakanese chronicles and writers such as D.G.E. Hall and Maurice Collis, and appendices follow.

A Burmese rebuttal of Rohingya accounts of history, written in 2003 by Rakhine writers in Japan in reply to the writings of the Rohingya activist Zaw Min Htut. The author argues that 'Rohingya' is a name taken up by Bengali Muslims after Burma's independence, that they are not an indigenous people of Arakan, and that their history is invented to support territorial claims. Across eight chapters it discusses Arakan's Muslims from the Mrauk-U period on, the 1942 communal violence, the Mujahid rebellion and immigration, and it ends with appendices and a bibliography.

The author argues that the British brought Chittagonian Bengali Muslims into Arakan as labourers, that they pushed out the Rakhine of Maungdaw and Buthidaung, and that the Mujahid rebellion was a separatist threat. It ends with a sketch map of Maungdaw town.

ဆရာခိုင်မျိုးစောင့် ရေးသားပြီး ဂျပန်နိုင်ငံရှိ ရခိုင်မျိုးစောင့်အုပ်စု (Arakan Rakhitta Group) က ၂၀၁၀ ခုနှစ်တွင် ထုတ်ဝေသော မြန်မာဘာသာ စာအုပ်ဖြစ်ပြီး ဒေါက်တာအေးချမ်း၏ အမှာစာ ပါဝင်သည်။ အပိုင်းနှစ်ပိုင်းတွင် ၁၉၄၈ နောက်ပိုင်း ပါလီမန်ဒီမိုကရေစီခေတ် ရခိုင်နိုင်ငံရေးနှင့် ဘူးသီးတောင်၊ မောင်တော အခြေအနေကို ဖော်ပြထားသည်။ စာရေးသူက ဗြိတိသျှတို့သည် စစ်တကောင်း ဘင်္ဂါလီမွတ်စလင်များကို လယ်ယာလုပ်သားများအဖြစ် ရခိုင်ပြည်သို့ ခေါ်ဆောင်လာခဲ့ကြောင်း၊ ၎င်းတို့က မောင်တောနှင့် ဘူးသီးတောင်ရှိ ရခိုင်များကို ဖယ်ရှားခဲ့ကြောင်းနှင့် မူဂျာဟစ်သူပုန်မှာ ခွဲထွက်ရေး ခြိမ်းခြောက်မှု ဖြစ်ကြောင်း စောဒကတက်သည်။ နောက်ဆုံးတွင် မောင်တောမြို့ မြေပုံကြမ်း ပါဝင်သည်။
Author        : ဆရာခိုင်မျိုးစောင့် (Saya Khaing Myo Saung)

edit.title: Influx Virus Rohingya
edit.mDescription:
Influx Viruses - The Illegal Muslims in Arakan, a 2005 book by U Shwe Zan, a former immigration officer in Arakan, and the historian Dr Aye Chan, published by Arakanese in United States. The authors argue that the Rohingya are illegal Bengali Muslim immigrants rather than an ethnic group of Burma. U Shwe Zan's essay traces Muslim migration from the Mrauk-U period to the 1980s, and Aye Chan's essay, The Development of a Muslim Enclave in Arakan, covers colonial-era migration and communal violence with British census tables. A longer Burmese section follows.
Authors       : U Shwe Zan and Dr. Aye Chan
Year          : 2005
Language      : English and Burmese
Publisher     : Arakanese in United States, New York
ISBN          : 0-9728698-4-0
Pages         : 77
File Size     : 0.5 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Islamic terrorist attacked
edit.mDescription:
An anonymous English web compilation with photos, saved as a PDF in 2019. The author calls the Rohingya 'Bengali Muslims' and argues that the RSO and other Rohingya armed groups are terrorists trained by the Bangladeshi army and backed by the OIC and al-Qaeda. It retells, from the security forces' side, the November 2012 kidnapping of three Burmese army engineers and the January 2014 Du Chee Yar Tan incident in Maungdaw, and claims that Rohingya activists mislead the world. It cites blog posts and incanews.com.
Author        : Richard SCRIBD
Language      : English
Pages         : 20
File Size     : 3.4 MB

edit.title: အမျိူးပျောက်မှာစိုးကြောက်စရာ
edit.mDescription:
An anonymous Burmese anti-Muslim booklet whose title means 'fear that our race will disappear', circulated as an e-book in 2011. The author argues that Muslims in Burma aim to absorb the Buddhist peoples by marrying and converting Buddhist women and by using money, and warns that Buddhism and the indigenous races could vanish within a hundred years unless parents, teachers and religious groups act. It also tells how Islam spread in Afghanistan, Pakistan and Arakan, and ends with a poem by Zawgyi.

edit.title: အကြမ်းဖက်မှုတို့မြစ်ဖျားခံရာ
edit.mDescription:
A Burmese anti-Islam booklet, first published in December 2014, whose title means 'the source of terrorism'. The compilers argue that Islam itself is the root of terrorism. They quote numbered Quran verses about unbelievers in Burmese, set them beside articles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and surround them with photos of attacks and executions by groups such as ISIS and of violence in Rakhine State, which they blame on Muslims. A preface addressed to the people of Myanmar warns of a threat to Buddhism.

၂၀၁၄ ခုနှစ် ဒီဇင်ဘာလတွင် ပထမအကြိမ် ထုတ်ဝေသော မြန်မာဘာသာ အစ္စလာမ်ဆန့်ကျင်ရေး စာစောင်ဖြစ်ပြီး ခေါင်းစဉ်၏ အဓိပ္ပာယ်မှာ “အကြမ်းဖက်မှု၏ မူလအစ” ဖြစ်သည်။ ပြုစုသူများက အစ္စလာမ်ဘာသာ ကိုယ်တိုင်သည် အကြမ်းဖက်မှု၏ အရင်းအမြစ် ဖြစ်သည်ဟု စောဒကတက်သည်။ ဘာသာမဲ့များဆိုင်ရာ ကုရ်အာန်ကျမ်းချက်များကို မြန်မာဘာသာဖြင့် ကိုးကားကာ ကုလသမဂ္ဂ လူ့အခွင့်အရေး ကြေညာစာတမ်းပါ အပိုဒ်များနှင့် ယှဉ်ပြထားပြီး ISIS စသော အဖွဲ့များ၏ တိုက်ခိုက်မှု၊ ကွပ်မျက်မှု ဓာတ်ပုံများနှင့် မွတ်စလင်များကို အပြစ်ပုံချသော ရခိုင်ပြည်နယ် အကြမ်းဖက်မှု ဓာတ်ပုံများ ပါဝင်သည်။ မြန်မာပြည်သူများထံ ရည်ညွှန်းသော နိဒါန်းတွင် ဗုဒ္ဓသာသနာအပေါ် ခြိမ်းခြောက်မှုကို သတိပေးထားသည်။

edit.title: Tear times summer 2018
edit.mDescription:
The Summer 2018 issue of Tear Times, the supporters' magazine of the British Christian relief charity Tearfund, edited by Peter Shaw. Its cover story, A Tale of Two Floods, tells how Tearfund's Bangladesh team responded in 2017 to the South Asia floods and to the arrival of about 700,000 Rohingya refugees, with interviews in the Kutupalong-Balukhali camp. The rest of the issue covers Tearfund's work in Malawi, East Africa and Yemen, fundraising news and Christian reflections.
Author        : Tearfund
Editor        : Peter Shaw
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Publisher     : Tearfund, UK
Pages         : 32
File Size     : 6.1 MB

edit.title: The Maharani of Arakan
edit.mDescription:
A romantic comedy in one act by the English playwright George Calderon, based on Rabindranath Tagore's story Dalia and published in London in 1915. Set in Arakan after the Mughal prince Shah Shuja was killed there, it follows his daughters Amina and Roshenara, who live hidden with the boatman Tung Loo, and Amina's love for the young man Dalia, who turns out to be the King of Arakan. The book opens with a character sketch of Tagore by K. N. Das Gupta and has photographs from the Indian Art and Dramatic Society's London staging.
Author        : George Calderon
Year          : 1915
Language      : English
Publisher     : Francis Griffiths, London
Pages         : 104
File Size     : 2.9 MB

edit.title: Puisi(Poetry) Rohingya(in Malay Language) 08 2017
edit.mDescription:
Dukamu Rohingya (Your Sorrow, Rohingya), an anthology of humanitarian poetry in Indonesian, published in September 2017 as issue No. 3 of the Indonesian magazine Kultur by NeoKultur. The editors gathered poems first posted on Facebook by Indonesian writers in response to the violence against the Rohingya that August and September. It has 18 short poems by poets such as Ghouts Misra, Sugiono MP and Eko Windarto, with titles like Rohingya, Untuk Rohingya and Aung San Suu Kyi, set over news photographs and a map of Myanmar's ethnic groups.
Editor        : NeoKultur
Year          : 2017
Language      : Indonesian
Publisher     : NeoKultur (Kultur No. 3)
Pages         : 24

edit.title: JRP for Rohingya Humanitarian Crisis 2018
edit.mDescription:
The Joint Response Plan for March to December 2018, the humanitarian appeal of the UN agencies, NGOs and the Government of Bangladesh for the Rohingya refugees in Cox's Bazar. It describes the needs of about 1.3 million people, refugees who fled after 25 August 2017 and Bangladeshi host communities, sets four strategic objectives, and gives plans, targets and budgets for each sector, such as food, health, shelter, water and sanitation, protection and education. In total it asks for about US$951 million.
Author        : Strategic Executive Group and partners (Bangladesh)
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Pages         : 90
File Size     : 6.5 MB

edit.title: Suspended in time :The ongoing persecution of Rohingya
edit.mDescription:
A policy paper from the US Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF), published in December 2016. It examines how conditions for Rohingya Muslims in Rakhine State worsened from 2011 to mid-2016, under President Thein Sein and the first months of the NLD government, including the four race and religion laws, anti-Muslim hate speech, violence, displacement and denial of citizenship. It ends with recommendations to the governments of Burma and the United States.
Author        : US Commission on International Religious Freedom
Year          : 2016
Language      : English
Pages         : 22
File Size     : 0.6 MB

edit.title: Report on enviromental impact of Rohingya influx
edit.mDescription:
A report by UNDP Bangladesh and UN Women, published in March 2018, on the damage to the environment around the Rohingya camps in Cox's Bazar after the 2017 influx. Based on a rapid environmental impact assessment carried out in late 2017 with Bangladesh's Ministry of Environment and Forests, it covers the loss of forest, vegetation and wildlife, water shortages, sanitation and waste, and the dangers of cooking with firewood, with special attention to risks for women and girls. It recommends actions to restore the ecosystem.
Author        : UNDP Bangladesh and UN Women Bangladesh
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Publisher     : UNDP Bangladesh and UN Women, Dhaka
Pages         : 108
File Size     : 20.7 MB

edit.title: Rohingya crisis response children's consultation report
edit.mDescription:
A report by Save the Children, Plan International and World Vision, published in February 2018, based on a consultation with about 200 Rohingya refugee children and children from host communities in Cox's Bazar, aged 7 to 17, held in December 2017. Part one tells a day in the life of a child in the camps, and part two sets out what children said about their safety at night, lack of space to play and learn, illness, food, and privacy for girls. It ends with recommendations for a child-centred response.
Author        : Eline Severijnen and Linda Ridwan Steinbock (Save the Children)
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Publisher     : Save the Children International, Plan International and World Vision International
Pages         : 32
File Size     : 7.3 MB

edit.title: Rohingya refugee children face a perilous future
edit.mDescription:
A UNICEF Child Alert from October 2017, "Outcast and Desperate", on Rohingya children who fled violence in Myanmar after 25 August 2017 to camps in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh. With many photographs and children's own drawings, it describes what children saw and lost, and their needs for food, safe water, sanitation, vaccinations, education and counselling. An introduction by UNICEF's Executive Director Anthony Lake presents UNICEF's US$76.1 million appeal for 720,000 children.
Author        : UNICEF
Year          : 2017
Language      : English
Pages         : 32
File Size     : 5.4 MB

edit.title: We are at breaking point(Report by Amnesty International
edit.mDescription:
An Amnesty International report from December 2016 on the security operations in northern Rakhine State after the attacks on border police posts on 9 October 2016. Based on interviews with Rohingya in Myanmar and Bangladesh and on satellite images, it documents unlawful killings, arbitrary arrests, rape, the burning of homes and villages, and the blocking of aid, which it says may amount to crimes against humanity. It also covers pushbacks and lack of food and shelter for refugees in Bangladesh, and ends with recommendations.
Author        : Amnesty International
Year          : 2016
Language      : English
Publisher     : Amnesty International Ltd, London
Pages         : 62
File Size     : 4.7 MB

edit.title: ခိုးဝင်ဘင်္ဂလီ(သို့မဟုတ်) Rohingya Genocide
edit.mDescription:
An essay in Burmese by Aung Aung (Sittwe), "Illegal Bengali, or Rohingya Genocide". The author argues that the Rohingya are a long-established Muslim people of Arakan, tracing their history through the Arakan kingdom, the Burmese conquest, British rule, the Second World War and independence. He argues that military governments used Burman and Buddhist nationalism and the label "illegal Bengali" to take away their citizenship, especially through the 1982 law, and ends with the violence after the October 2016 attacks in Maungdaw, which he calls a systematic genocide. Sources are listed in endnotes.

စစ်တွေမှ အောင်အောင် ရေးသားသော “ခိုးဝင်ဘင်္ဂါလီ (သို့မဟုတ်) Rohingya Genocide” ဆောင်းပါးဖြစ်သည်။ ရိုဟင်ဂျာများသည် ရခိုင်ဒေသတွင် ရှေးယခင်ကတည်းက နေထိုင်လာသော မွတ်စလင်လူမျိုးဖြစ်ကြောင်း ရခိုင်ဘုရင့်နိုင်ငံခေတ်၊ မြန်မာဘုရင်၏ သိမ်းပိုက်မှု၊ ဗြိတိသျှခေတ်၊ ဒုတိယကမ္ဘာစစ်နှင့် လွတ်လပ်ရေးရပြီးခေတ်များကို ဖော်ပြကာ စာရေးသူက ဆွေးနွေးထားသည်။ စစ်အစိုးရများသည် အမျိုးသားရေးဝါဒ၊ ဗုဒ္ဓဘာသာအမျိုးသားရေးဝါဒနှင့် “ခိုးဝင်ဘင်္ဂါလီ” ဟူသော အမည်ကို အသုံးပြု၍ အထူးသဖြင့် ၁၉၈၂ နိုင်ငံသားဥပဒေဖြင့် ရိုဟင်ဂျာတို့၏ နိုင်ငံသားအခွင့်အရေးကို ဖယ်ရှားခဲ့သည်ဟု စာရေးသူက ဆိုသည်။ ၂၀၁၆ ခုနှစ် အောက်တိုဘာလ မောင်တောတိုက်ခိုက်မှုနောက်ပိုင်း အကြမ်းဖက်မှုများကို စနစ်တကျ လူမျိုးတုံးသတ်ဖြတ်မှုဟု ဖော်ပြကာ နိဂုံးချုပ်ထားပြီး ကိုးကားချက်များကို နောက်ဆုံးတွင် ဖော်ပြထားသည်။
Author        : Aung Aung (Sittwe)
Language      : Burmese

edit.title: Rakhine Rohingya conflict analysis
edit.mDescription:
A university student paper by Min Zaw, written for a course in conflict analysis, that maps the 2012 violence between Rakhine Buddhists and Rohingya Muslims in Rakhine State. Using a conflict-mapping model, it looks at the parties involved, the history of their relationship, cultural and economic causes, the spiral of attacks and revenge, and the role of monks, political parties, security forces, aid groups and the media. It ends with ideas for peace-building, first ending violence and then tackling discrimination and inequality.
Author        : Min Zaw
Year          : 2014
Language      : English
Pages         : 22
File Size     : 1.0 MB

edit.title: National Verification Cards: A Barrier to Rohingya Repatriation
edit.mDescription:
A 2019 report by the Burma Human Rights Network on the National Verification Card (NVC), the identity card Myanmar's authorities require the Rohingya to accept. Based on interviews with 25 Rohingya in Rakhine State and the Bangladesh camps between February and June 2019, it explains the 1982 citizenship law, the White Cards and the yearly household surveys, and finds that the NVC denies the Rohingya their identity and does not end restrictions on travel. It argues that the cards must not be a condition for refugees to return home.
Author        : Richard Potter, Kyaw Win
Editor        : Thomas MacManus and Ronan Lee
Year          : 2019
Language      : English
Publisher     : Burma Human Rights Network (BHRN)
Pages         : 31
File Size     : 2.5 MB

edit.title: "We Will Destroy Everything": Military Responsibility for Crimes against Humanity in Rakhine State
edit.mDescription:
A major Amnesty International report from June 2018 on the Myanmar military's campaign against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State in 2017. Based on more than 400 interviews, satellite images and other evidence, it documents arrests and torture, large massacres, rape, landmines, forced starvation and the burning and bulldozing of villages, and also covers attacks by the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA). It explains the army's chain of command and names 13 officers, including Senior General Min Aung Hlaing, who should face trial for crimes against humanity.
Author        : Amnesty International
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Publisher     : Amnesty International Ltd, London
Pages         : 186
File Size     : 7.5 MB

edit.title: BRAC Annual Report 2017
edit.mDescription:
The annual report of BRAC, the Bangladeshi development organisation, for the year 2017. Its cover story is told by Keya, a 13-year-old Rohingya girl in Cox's Bazar, and a section on humanitarian crisis management describes BRAC's work for Rohingya refugees after August 2017, such as health centres, learning centres, latrines, wells and shelters. The rest covers BRAC's programmes in Bangladesh and abroad on poverty, finance, skills, health, gender, education and climate, with its management and financial statements.
Author        : BRAC
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Publisher     : BRAC, Dhaka
Pages         : 116
File Size     : 36.5 MB

edit.title: Human Rights Abuses and Discrimination on Rohingyas
edit.mDescription:
A book by Zaw Min Htut, president of the Burmese Rohingya Association in Japan, compiled largely from the records and writings of A. F. K. Jilani and first published in 2003. It describes decades of abuse against the Rohingya of Arakan, including the citizenship law, the refugee exoduses of 1978, 1991-92, 1996 and 1997, conditions in the Bangladesh camps, new settlements in Arakan, forced labour, limits on religious freedom and the 2001 violence in Akyab (Sittwe). A second part covers Rohingya in Japan and BRAJ's letters to the UN, Japan and the EU.
Author        : Zaw Min Htut
Year          : 2003
Language      : English
Publisher     : Burmese Rohingya Association in Japan (BRAJ), Tokyo
ISBN          : 984-32-0956-7

File Size     : 7.5 MB

edit.title: Dignity and the displaced Rohingya in Bangladesh
edit.mDescription:
An HPG working paper from August 2018, part of an ODI study on dignity in displacement. Based on interviews with Rohingya refugees in Cox's Bazar in April and May 2018, it explains what dignity (ijjot) means to the Rohingya in social, religious and economic terms, and compares this with how aid agencies use the word. It looks at refugees' views of aid, respectful treatment by volunteers, gender, cash and the variety of distributions, and what a dignified return to Myanmar would mean.
Authors       : Kerrie Holloway and Lilianne Fan
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Publisher     : Humanitarian Policy Group, Overseas Development Institute (ODI), London
