edit.title: A History of Shielding Abusers
edit.mDescription:
A short Human Rights Watch paper from September 2018 that reviews the commissions Myanmar set up to investigate violence in Rakhine State since 2012, at least eight in all. It explains how each one, from the 2012 Inquiry Commission to those formed after the 2016 and 2017 attacks, lacked independence, avoided naming those responsible and led to no real justice for the Rohingya. It urges the UN Human Rights Council to create an independent international mechanism to collect and preserve evidence for future prosecutions.
Author        : Human Rights Watch
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Pages         : 8
File Size     : 0.1 MB

edit.title: Country Policy and Information Note  Burma: Rohingya
edit.mDescription:
Guidance and country information from the UK Home Office (version 1.0, November 2017) for officials deciding asylum claims by Rohingya from Burma. It summarises evidence on the origin of the name Rohingya, population, language, citizenship and identity documents, marriage rules, the October 2016 and August 2017 violence, Buddhist nationalism, displacement camps, and limits on movement, education and health care. Its policy conclusion is that the discrimination faced by Rohingya in Rakhine State in general amounts to persecution.
Author        : UK Home Office
Year          : 2017
Language      : English
Pages         : 50
File Size     : 1.0 MB

edit.title: Myanmars armed forces and the rohingya crisis
edit.mDescription:
A study by Andrew Selth, an Australian expert on Myanmar's military, published by the United States Institute of Peace (Peaceworks No. 140, August 2018). It looks at the Tatmadaw's organisation, training, ethos and chain of command to ask who would be responsible for the 2016 and 2017 clearance operations against the Rohingya if the case came before an international court. It also covers the international reaction and how the crisis has harmed everyone in Myanmar, and concludes that a fair solution and legal accounting remain distant.
Author        : Andrew Selth
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Publisher     : United States Institute of Peace, Washington DC
ISBN          : 978-1-60127-725-1
Pages         : 56
File Size     : 3.2 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Briefing Report
edit.mDescription:
A short briefing report by Warzone Initiatives from October 2015, written as an introduction for general readers. It covers the history of Myanmar (colonial rule, Buddhism and ethnic conflict), the history of the Rohingya, their situation before the 2015 elections, and the responses of neighbouring and Western countries. It then looks at Myanmar's laws such as the 1982 Citizenship Law, at international law, and asks whether the treatment of the Rohingya amounts to crimes against humanity, ethnic cleansing or genocide. A timeline is included.
Author        : Warzone Initiatives
Year          : 2015
Language      : English
Pages         : 20
File Size     : 3.2 MB

edit.title: Rohingyas in India : Birth of a stateless community
edit.mDescription:
Issue 71 of the Policies and Practices series of the Calcutta Research Group, published in September 2015, with three research papers on Rohingya in India. The first, by Suchismita Majumder, looks at Rohingya held in jails and correctional homes in West Bengal after crossing from Bangladesh. The second, by Priyanca Mathur Velath and Kriti Chopra, studies the Rohingya community in Hyderabad. The third, by Madhura Chakraborty, compares the treatment of stateless Rohingya in Myanmar, Bangladesh and India.
Author        : Suchismita Majumder, Priyanca Mathur Velath, Kriti Chopra and Madhura Chakraborty
Year          : 2015
Language      : English
Publisher     : Mahanirban Calcutta Research Group, Kolkata
Pages         : 60
File Size     : 5.6 MB

edit.title: Special feature Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh the humanitarian response
edit.mDescription:
Issue 73 of Humanitarian Exchange, the magazine of the Humanitarian Practice Network at ODI, published in October 2018 as a special feature on the aid response to the Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh. Its 13 short articles by aid workers and researchers cover the political context, statelessness, trafficking, UNHCR's past handling of Rohingya returns in the 1970s and 1990s, local leadership, dignity, communication with refugees, monsoon preparedness, health care in the mega-camp, and mapping the camps.
Author        : Humanitarian Practice Network (HPN)
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Publisher     : Overseas Development Institute (ODI), London
Pages         : 44
File Size     : 4.2 MB

edit.title: The Rohingya Crises in Bangladesh and Burma
edit.mDescription:
A report for the United States Congress by the Congressional Research Service, dated 8 November 2017 (R45016). It explains the events after the August 2017 attacks in Rakhine State that drove more than 600,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh, the background of the Rohingya and Burma's discriminatory laws, the humanitarian situation on both sides of the border, and the problems of repatriation. It also discusses the Annan Commission, the risk of radicalisation, the US response and aid, and two bills on Burma before Congress.
Author        : Michael F. Martin, Rhoda Margesson and Bruce Vaughn (Congressional Research Service)
Year          : 2017
Language      : English
Publisher     : Congressional Research Service, Washington DC
Pages         : 34
File Size     : 1.4 MB

edit.title: Myanmar-the-politics-of-rakhine-state
edit.mDescription:
International Crisis Group Asia Report No. 261, "Myanmar - The Politics of Rakhine State", published on 22 October 2014. It traces the history of Rakhine State, then describes poverty, the 2012 violence, the status of Muslims and the humanitarian situation. It sets out the grievances and politics of the Rakhine Buddhists and the views of the Rohingya and Kaman Muslims, including the citizenship verification process, and looks at radicalisation, the Bangladesh border and regional concerns before suggesting a way forward on citizenship and the Rakhine State Action Plan.
Author        : International Crisis Group
Year          : 2014
Language      : English
Publisher     : International Crisis Group, Brussels
Pages         : 48
File Size     : 2.7 MB

edit.title: All you can do is pray
edit.mDescription:
A Human Rights Watch report from April 2013 on the violence against Rohingya Muslims in Arakan (Rakhine) State in 2012. It describes calls by local leaders and monks to drive Muslims out after the June 2012 violence, the coordinated attacks of October 2012 including the massacre in Yan Thei village, mass graves, arrests, and the destruction of homes and mosques, and finds these amount to crimes against humanity and ethnic cleansing. It also covers aid restrictions, displacement, denial of citizenship and the government's response, with recommendations.
Author        : Human Rights Watch
Year          : 2013
Language      : English
Publisher     : Human Rights Watch
ISBN          : 978-1-62313-0053
Pages         : 165
File Size     : 32.0 MB

edit.title: Myanmar's Crime against Humanity
edit.mDescription:
A paper by Aung Aung (Sittwe), subtitled "State Policy to Annihilate Rohingya", which argues that Myanmar's treatment of the Rohingya is a crime against humanity and genocide. Chapters cover the Rohingya's claim to citizenship and rights, the history and Islamic heritage of Arakan, the 1942 massacre, evidence for the name Rohingya, the 1982 Citizenship Law, anti-Muslim propaganda, the 2012 violence and blockade, and a call for a UN commission of inquiry. Long references are illustrated with photographs of documents and old mosques.
Author        : Aung Aung (Sittwe)
Language      : English
Pages         : 52
File Size     : 10.6 MB

edit.title: The Slow Burning Genocide Of Myanmar's Rohingya
edit.mDescription:
An academic article by Maung Zarni and Alice Cowley, published in the Pacific Rim Law & Policy Journal (vol. 23, no. 3, 2014). Based on three years of research, it argues that since the 1978 Nagamin operation the Myanmar state has carried out a slow-burning genocide against the Rohingya, through stripping their citizenship and identity, restrictions on marriage and births, hate campaigns and the 2012 violence, and that four of the five acts of genocide in the 1948 Genocide Convention have been committed. It also criticises the international community's silence.
Author        : Maung Zarni and Alice Cowley
Year          : 2014
Language      : English
Publisher     : Pacific Rim Law & Policy Journal Association
Pages         : 72
File Size     : 0.4 MB

edit.title: PERSECUTION OF THE ROHINGYA MUSLIMS
edit.mDescription:
A legal analysis prepared by the human rights clinic at Yale Law School for Fortify Rights, published in October 2015. It first gives a detailed history of abuses against the Rohingya since Myanmar's independence, including denial of citizenship, forced labour, marriage restrictions, the 2012 violence and conditions in the displacement camps. It then tests these facts against each element of the 1948 Genocide Convention and finds strong evidence that genocide is taking place, and discusses the state's responsibility and duty to prevent it.
Author        : Allard K. Lowenstein International Human Rights Clinic, Yale Law School (for Fortify Rights)
Year          : 2015
Language      : English
Pages         : 78
File Size     : 3.0 MB

edit.title: Everywhere is Trouble
edit.mDescription:
A briefing by Fortify Rights and the Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK on Rohingya refugees in Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia, about ten months after the May 2015 Andaman Sea boat crisis. Based on a visit to the three countries in February and March 2016, it describes long detention of refugees and children in Thailand, human trafficking, lack of asylum and UNHCR registration, police abuse and labour exploitation in Malaysia, and camp conditions in Aceh, Indonesia. It also reports how Indonesian officials forced BROUK's president Tun Khin to leave the country.
Author        : Fortify Rights and Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK)
Year          : 2016
Language      : English
Pages         : 20
File Size     : 2.1 MB

edit.title: Genocide of the Rohingya of Myanmar in 2012
edit.mDescription:
A special issue of ARNO's Arakan magazine, released on 20 January 2013, with an essay by Dr. Habib Siddiqui on the 2012 violence against the Rohingya. The author argues that the attacks of June and October 2012 in Sittwe, Mrauk-U, Kyaukphyu and other towns were a planned genocidal campaign backed by officials and security forces. He lists military operations against the Rohingya since 1948 and compares monks' calls to boycott Muslims with Nazi Germany's laws. It ends with an ARNO appeal for UN peacekeepers and a commission of inquiry, and many photographs, some very graphic.
Author        : Dr. Habib Siddiqui
Editor        : M. A. Alam
Year          : 2013
Language      : English
Publisher     : Arakan Rohingya National Organisation (ARNO)
Pages         : 35
File Size     : 2.3 MB

edit.title: ဒူချီးရာတန်းအစီရင်ခံစာ
edit.mDescription:
The report, in Burmese, of the 10-member commission led by Dr. Tha Hla Shwe that Myanmar's President appointed in February 2014 to investigate events of January 2014 in Du Chee Yar Tan village tract, Maungdaw Township, where a police sergeant went missing and the UN reported killings of Rohingya villagers. After interviewing 175 people, the commission concluded that the sergeant was probably killed by villagers but found no reliable evidence for the reported killings of villagers. It also reviews UN and media reports and makes recommendations on security, citizenship and peace in Rakhine State.

၂၀၁၄ ခုနှစ် ဇန်နဝါရီလတွင် မောင်တောမြို့နယ် ဒူချီးရာတန်းကျေးရွာအုပ်စု၌ ဖြစ်ပွားခဲ့သော အဖြစ်အပျက်များကို စုံစမ်းရန် နိုင်ငံတော်သမ္မတက ၂၀၁၄ ခုနှစ် ဖေဖော်ဝါရီလတွင် ဖွဲ့စည်းခဲ့သော ဒေါက်တာသာလှရွှေ ဦးဆောင်သည့် (၁၀) ဦးပါ စုံစမ်းစစ်ဆေးရေးကော်မရှင်၏ အစီရင်ခံစာဖြစ်သည်။ ကော်မရှင်သည် မောင်တောသို့ ကွင်းဆင်းကာ လူ (၁၇၅) ဦးကို မေးမြန်းခဲ့ပြီး ပျောက်ဆုံးသွားသော ရဲတပ်ကြပ်ကြီးတစ်ဦးမှာ ရွာသားများ၏ တိုက်ခိုက်မှုကြောင့် သေဆုံးနိုင်သည်ဟု ကောက်ချက်ချသော်လည်း ရွာသားများ သေဆုံးသည်ဟူသော သတင်းများအတွက် ခိုင်လုံသော အထောက်အထား မတွေ့ရှိကြောင်း ဖော်ပြထားသည်။ ကုလသမဂ္ဂ၊ မီဒီယာနှင့် Facebook သတင်းများကို သုံးသပ်ထားပြီး လုံခြုံရေး၊ ၁၉၈၂ ခုနှစ် နိုင်ငံသားဥပဒေနှင့် ရခိုင်ပြည်နယ် ငြိမ်းချမ်းရေးဆိုင်ရာ အကြံပြုချက်များ ပါဝင်သည်။
Author        : Investigation Commission on Du Chee Yar Tan (chair Dr. Tha Hla Shwe)
Year          : 2014
Language      : Burmese
Pages         : 110
File Size     : 6.7 MB

edit.title: Rakhine Conflict and Peaceful Co Exitance
edit.mDescription:
A paper in Burmese compiled by Maung Ye Chan, "Rakhine Conflict and Peaceful Co-existence", written after the 2012 violence in Rakhine State. It sets out how Rakhine Buddhists and Muslims each see the conflict, then answers common Rakhine claims using chronicles, history and population data, arguing that Rakhine has long been a multi-ethnic, multi-religious society. It proposes a win-win approach of development, education and dialogue. About 30 pages of appendices reproduce British colonial records from the 1820s and Buchanan's 1799 word list of the language of the "Rooinga".

၂၀၁၂ ခုနှစ် ရခိုင်ပြည်နယ် အဓိကရုဏ်းများနောက်ပိုင်း မောင်ရဲချမ်း ပြုစုတင်ပြသော “ရခိုင်ဒေသပဋိပက္ခနှင့် ငြိမ်းချမ်းစွာ အတူနေထိုင်ရေး” စာတမ်းဖြစ်သည်။ ပဋိပက္ခအပေါ် ရခိုင်အမျိုးသားများ၏ အမြင်နှင့် မွတ်စလင်များ၏ အမြင်ကို ဖော်ပြပြီး ရခိုင်ဘက်မှ ပြောဆိုချက်များကို ရာဇဝင်၊ သမိုင်းနှင့် လူဦးရေ အချက်အလက်များဖြင့် ပြန်လည်သုံးသပ်ကာ ရခိုင်ဒေသသည် ရှေးယခင်ကတည်းက လူမျိုးစုံ ဘာသာစုံ နေထိုင်ရာ ဒေသဖြစ်ကြောင်း စာရေးသူက ဆွေးနွေးထားသည်။ ဖွံ့ဖြိုးရေး၊ ပညာရေးနှင့် ဆွေးနွေးညှိနှိုင်းမှုဖြင့် နှစ်ဖက်စလုံး အကျိုးရှိမည့် နည်းလမ်းကို အကြံပြုထားသည်။ နောက်ဆက်တွဲတွင် ၁၈၂၀ ပြည့်နှစ်များမှ ဗြိတိသျှ မှတ်တမ်းများနှင့် ၁၇၉၉ ခုနှစ် Buchanan ၏ “Rooinga” ဘာသာစကား ဝေါဟာရစာရင်းတို့ကို ထည့်သွင်းထားသည်။
Author        : Maung Ye Chan
Language      : Burmese
Pages         : 50
File Size     : 14.2 MB

edit.title: Rohingya by ABSDF
edit.mDescription:
A typed study paper in Burmese by the research department of the All Burma Students' Democratic Front (ABSDF), dated 7 June 1992, on "the Rohingya problem and the problem of refugees on the Myanmar-Bangladesh border". Part one explains the Rohingya question, their history, three different views of whether they are an ethnic group, citizens or foreigners, and Rohingya armed groups. Part two describes the refugees who fled to Bangladesh in 1991-92, international pressure, talks between the two governments, and the uncertain future of the refugees.

မြန်မာနိုင်ငံလုံးဆိုင်ရာ ကျောင်းသားများ ဒီမိုကရက်တစ်တပ်ဦး (ABSDF) ဗဟိုကော်မတီဌာနချုပ် သုတေသနဌာနခွဲက ၁၉၉၂ ခုနှစ် ဇွန်လ (၇) ရက်စွဲဖြင့် ပြုစုသော “ရိုဟင်ဂျာပြဿနာနှင့် မြန်မာ-ဘင်္ဂလားဒေ့ရှ် နယ်စပ်ဒုက္ခသည်များ ပြဿနာအပေါ် လေ့လာချက်စာတမ်း” ဖြစ်သည်။ ပထမပိုင်းတွင် ရိုဟင်ဂျာပြဿနာ၊ ရိုဟင်ဂျာတို့၏ သမိုင်း၊ ၎င်းတို့သည် တိုင်းရင်းသားလူမျိုးစု၊ နိုင်ငံသား သို့မဟုတ် နိုင်ငံခြားသားဖြစ်သည်ဟူသော အမြင်သုံးမျိုးနှင့် ရိုဟင်ဂျာလက်နက်ကိုင်အဖွဲ့များကို ဆွေးနွေးထားသည်။ ဒုတိယပိုင်းတွင် ၁၉၉၁-၉၂ ခုနှစ်တွင် ဘင်္ဂလားဒေ့ရှ်သို့ ထွက်ပြေးခဲ့သော ဒုက္ခသည်များ၏ အခြေအနေ၊ နိုင်ငံတကာ၏ ဖိအားပေးမှု၊ နှစ်နိုင်ငံ ဆွေးနွေးမှုများနှင့် ဒုက္ခသည်များ၏ အနာဂတ်ကို ဖော်ပြထားသည်။
Author        : All Burma Students' Democratic Front (ABSDF), Research Department
Year          : 1992

Pages         : 49

edit.title: Countdown to Annihilation: Genocide in Myanmar
edit.mDescription:
A research report by the International State Crime Initiative at Queen Mary University of London, published in 2015 and based on fieldwork in Rakhine State. It argues that the Rohingya are in the later stages of a genocidal process and follows its stages, from stigmatisation and dehumanisation (citizenship, the white cards, the hate preaching of monks and the 969 and Ma Ba Tha movements) to harassment and the June 2012 massacres, segregation in camps and the Aung Mingalar ghetto, and systematic weakening through hunger and denial of health care. It also includes leaked government documents.
Author        : Penny Green, Thomas MacManus, Alicia de la Cour Venning
Year          : 2015
Language      : English

edit.title: Final Report of Inquiry Commission on Sectarian Violence in Rakhine State
edit.mDescription:
The English version of the final report, dated 8 July 2013, of the commission led by Dr. Myo Myint that President Thein Sein set up in August 2012 after the violence in Rakhine State. It gives the commission's account of the state's history, the two phases of the 2012 violence, their causes, and the deaths and damage, with recommendations on the economy, basic needs, the rule of law, aid agencies and the media. The commission uses the term "Bengali" and explains why it rejects the name Rohingya.

edit.title: "All of My Body Was Pain": Sexual Violence against Rohingya Women and Girls in Burma
edit.mDescription:
A Human Rights Watch report from November 2017 on rape and other sexual violence by Burmese security forces against Rohingya women and girls during the attacks that began on 25 August 2017. Based on 52 interviews with women and girls in the Bangladesh camps, including 29 rape survivors, it documents gang rapes, the killing of family members, the hardships of pregnant women and survivors while fleeing, and the lack of medical care afterwards. It ends with recommendations to Burma, Bangladesh and the UN.

edit.title: "Are We Not Human?": Denial of Education for Rohingya Refugee Children in Bangladesh
edit.mDescription:
A Human Rights Watch report from December 2019 on how the Bangladesh government denies education to nearly 400,000 school-age Rohingya refugee children in the Cox's Bazar camps. It documents the ban on formal, accredited schooling in the camps, the barriers to local schools and national exams, and the limits of the informal learning centres, such as short hours, no full curriculum, poor quality and mixed ages. It links the policy to Bangladesh's push for repatriation and calls on the government, UNICEF and donors to allow certified education.

edit.title: "Bangladesh Is Not My Country": The Plight of Rohingya Refugees from Myanmar
edit.mDescription:
A Human Rights Watch report from August 2018 on the Rohingya refugees in the Cox's Bazar camps a year after the 2017 exodus. It describes the dangers of the overcrowded mega-camp, such as landslides and floods in the monsoon, physical insecurity, water and sanitation, food, fuel and health care, and the needs of older and disabled refugees. It also covers refugees' legal status and freedom of movement, obstacles to safe return to Myanmar, the plan to move refugees to Bhasan Char, and the need for education and livelihoods.

edit.title: "Let Us Speak for Our Rights": Human Rights Situation of Rohingya Refugees in Bangladesh
edit.mDescription:
A short Amnesty International report from 2020 on the human rights of Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh during the COVID-19 pandemic, built around refugees' own voices. Short chapters cover internet restrictions, violence against women, detention of refugees on Bhasan Char island, the lack of education, health care, relations with host communities, barbed-wire fences around the camps, and more than 100 apparent extrajudicial killings of refugees. It includes a timeline from 2017 to 2020 and recommendations to Bangladesh and the international community.

edit.title: "My Tears Could Make a Sea": The Infliction of Mental Harm as Genocide
edit.mDescription:
A 2024 report by Fortify Rights and the human rights clinic at Yale Law School arguing that the serious mental harm inflicted on the Rohingya is itself an act of genocide under the Genocide Convention. It draws on survivors' testimonies and a survey of refugees in the Bangladesh camps, carried out by a Rohingya research team, on trauma, depression, anxiety and daily functioning. It explains the law on mental harm as genocide, applies it to the Rohingya, and makes recommendations to Myanmar's rulers, Bangladesh, the International Criminal Court, the UN and ASEAN.
Author        : Fortify Rights and Allard K. Lowenstein International Human Rights Clinic (Yale Law School)

edit.title: "My World Is Finished": Rohingya Targeted in Crimes against Humanity in Myanmar
edit.mDescription:
An Amnesty International briefing from October 2017 on the Myanmar military's campaign against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State after the ARSA attacks of 25 August 2017, which in seven weeks drove more than half a million Rohingya into Bangladesh. Based on more than 150 interviews and satellite images, it documents unlawful killings of hundreds of women, men and children, rape and other sexual violence, and the organised burning of whole villages, and concludes that these are crimes against humanity. It ends with recommendations.
Author        : Amnesty International
Year          : 2017
Language      : English
Publisher     : Amnesty International Ltd, London

edit.mDescription:
A Physicians for Human Rights report from July 2018 on the massacre in the Rohingya village of Chut Pyin, northern Rakhine State, on 27 August 2017, when security forces and local Rakhine men killed or disappeared an estimated 400 villagers, including 99 children, and burned the village. PHR doctors interviewed and medically examined 22 survivors in Bangladesh, and their gunshot wounds, stab wounds and other injuries support the survivors' accounts. It includes detailed case profiles, a legal analysis calling for investigation of crimes against humanity, and recommendations.

edit.title: "Shot While Fleeing": Rohingya Disabled by Myanmar Authorities' Targeted Violence
edit.mDescription:
A Physicians for Human Rights report from June 2019 on Rohingya survivors left disabled by the violence of August 2017 in northern Rakhine State. PHR interviewed 114 survivors in the Bangladesh camps; doctors examined 90 who had been injured and found that 43 were left with long-term disabilities, most of them shot while fleeing. It describes their injuries and lasting nerve damage, analyses the attacks under human rights law, reviews Myanmar's response, and gives recommendations and detailed survivor profiles.

edit.title: "The Government Could Have Stopped This": Sectarian Violence and Ensuing Abuses in Burma's Arakan State
edit.mDescription:
A Human Rights Watch report from August 2012 on the sectarian violence between Arakan (Rakhine) Buddhists and Rohingya Muslims that began in June 2012 in Arakan State. It describes the killings on both sides, how police and soldiers stood by or joined in, and the abuses that followed against the Rohingya, such as killings, mass arrests, destruction of homes and mosques, forced relocation and blocked aid. It also covers the denial of citizenship and Bangladesh's pushing back of refugees, and gives recommendations.
Author        : Human Rights Watch
Year          : 2012
Language      : English
Publisher     : Human Rights Watch

edit.title: "The Torture in My Mind": The Right to Mental Health for Rohingya Survivors of Genocide
edit.mDescription:
A Fortify Rights report from December 2020 on the mental health of Rohingya genocide survivors in the Bangladesh camps, researched from 2018 to 2020 by a team of ten Rohingya refugee researchers. Based on 495 household surveys, focus groups and community workshops, it finds very high rates of depression (88.7 percent), emotional distress and PTSD, linked to atrocities in Myanmar and to restrictions in the camps. It covers views on return to Myanmar, analyses the right to mental health under international law, and makes recommendations, including referral of Myanmar to the ICC.

Year          : 2020

edit.title: "They Gave Them Long Swords": Preparations for Genocide and Crimes against Humanity
edit.mDescription:
A Fortify Rights report from July 2018 showing how Myanmar's authorities prepared the attacks on the Rohingya in the months before 25 August 2017, by taking away sharp tools from Rohingya, arming and training non-Rohingya locals, cutting food and aid, and building up troops. It then documents the killings, rape, burning and displacement by security forces and civilians after the militant attacks, as well as abuses by Rohingya militants. It argues these are genocide and crimes against humanity and names 22 army and police officials who should be criminally investigated.

Year          : 2018

edit.title: "They Tried to Kill Us All": Atrocity Crimes against Rohingya Muslims
edit.mDescription:
A joint "Bearing Witness" report from November 2017 by the Simon-Skjodt Center of the US Holocaust Memorial Museum and Fortify Rights on the clearance operations that followed the militant attacks of October 2016 and August 2017 in northern Rakhine State. Based on eyewitness testimony and satellite images, it documents mass killings, rape, mass arrests and the burning of villages that displaced nearly 700,000 Rohingya. It finds crimes against humanity and ethnic cleansing and growing evidence of genocide, reviews Myanmar's denials and commissions, and proposes next steps.

edit.title: "They Want Us All to Go Away": Early Warning Signs of Genocide in Burma
edit.mDescription:
A short illustrated report by the Simon-Skjodt Center for the Prevention of Genocide at the US Holocaust Memorial Museum, after its staff visited Burma in March 2015. Drawing on visits to the internment camps and the Aung Mingalar ghetto in Sittwe and on talks with Rohingya, it lists early warning signs of genocide, such as hate speech, segregation, loss of citizenship, blocked aid, and limits on movement, marriage, religion and education. It warns that the Rohingya are at grave risk of mass atrocities, including genocide, and urges action to prevent them.

edit.mDescription:

It traces the history of refugees in Malaysia, the reasons people flee Myanmar, Malaysian law, policy and practice, and the informal protection and difficulties of refugees living in cities such as Kuala Lumpur. It ends with policy recommendations for future refugee management.

edit.mDescription:
A four-page policy brief from April 2018 by Cindy Huang of the Center for Global Development. It proposes a refugee compact for Bangladesh, which hosts about 900,000 Rohingya in Cox's Bazar, combining long-term aid with policy reforms such as legal status, freedom of movement, education and the right to work. Drawing lessons from the Jordan Compact, it suggests "beyond aid" benefits for Bangladesh, such as extended trade preferences with the EU and more jobs abroad for Bangladeshi workers.

edit.mDescription:
A Refugees International field report by Daniel P. Sullivan, February 2020, on how Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh are left out of decisions about their own lives and future. It describes repatriation agreements and attempts made without consulting them, fear over plans to move 100,000 refugees to Bhasan Char island, the limits of the majhi leader system, and the rise of Rohingya civil society groups and the crackdown on them. It recommends real consultation and community representation in the camps.

edit.mDescription:
A Refugees International field report by Daniel P. Sullivan, April 2019, based on interviews in February and April 2019 with Rohingya who had just arrived in Bangladesh. It shows that the Rohingya still in Rakhine State face harassment, arbitrary arrest, forced labour and limits on movement and aid, made worse by fighting with the Arakan Army, while 120,000 remain in camps since 2012. It also covers the National Verification Card, impunity and options for justice, US policy, and the need to include Rohingya in repatriation talks.

edit.mDescription:
An open-access academic book edited by Anthony Ware and Monique Skidmore and published by ANU Press in 2023, with 15 chapters by different scholars on Myanmar after the military coup of 1 February 2021. Chapters cover scenarios for the future, social media activism, foreign business, international courts, China and ASEAN, the Federal Democracy Charter, aid, the pandemic and higher education. Two chapters focus on Rakhine State, on the Arakan Army's state-building and what it means for the Rohingya, and on communal tensions after the coup.

edit.mDescription:
A Human Rights Watch report from June 2021 on Bangladesh's relocation of Rohingya refugees from the Cox's Bazar camps to Bhasan Char, a remote silt island in the Bay of Bengal. It documents relocations without free and informed consent, people rescued from boats held on the island, broken promises of education and livelihoods, poor health care, food shortages, abuses by security forces and the risk of cyclones. edit.mDescription:
A Human Rights Watch report from October 2020 on the roughly 130,000 Rohingya and Kaman Muslims held since 2012 in camps in central Rakhine State. It describes the camps as open-air prisons, with tight limits on movement, arbitrary detention and extortion, squalid conditions, little health care, few livelihoods, denial of education and restricted aid. It examines citizenship and the National Verification Card, argues that the government's camp "closures" entrench apartheid, and finds the detention amounts to crimes against humanity.

edit.title: Bangladesh/Myanmar: The Dangers of a Rohingya Insurgency
edit.mDescription:
International Crisis Group Asia Report No. 348, published on 18 June 2025, on Rohingya armed groups after the Arakan Army took control of most of northern Rakhine State. It explains how these groups, which had fought each other in the Bangladesh camps and then sided with the Myanmar military, agreed in November 2024 to fight the Arakan Army together and stepped up recruitment of refugees. It warns that an insurgency would harm communal relations and chances of return, and urges Bangladesh to curb the groups and talk with the Arakan Army.

edit.mDescription:
A Refugees International policy brief from October 2017, based on a September 2017 visit to Bangladesh by its president Eric Schwartz and Daniel Sullivan, and adapted from Sullivan's testimony to the US Congress. It describes the Myanmar military's campaign of ethnic cleansing that drove more than 500,000 Rohingya out in a month, with burning, killing and rape, as crimes against humanity. It also covers the background of persecution, the overwhelmed aid response in the Cox's Bazar settlements, and recommendations for pressure on Myanmar and more aid.

edit.title: Breaking Away: The Battle for Myanmar's Rakhine State
edit.mDescription:
International Crisis Group Asia Report No. 339, published on 27 August 2024, on the Arakan Army's offensive since late 2023 that has taken most of central and northern Rakhine State. It describes the three-way conflict in which the military conscripted Rohingya and the Arakan Army is accused of abuses against Rohingya civilians, the role of the Bangladesh refugee camps and government, and the economic, humanitarian and governance challenges of the Arakan Army's emerging proto-state. It recommends dialogue with Rohingya leaders, investigations and wider aid.

edit.title: Buddhism and State Power in Myanmar
edit.mDescription:
International Crisis Group Asia Report No. 290, published on 5 September 2017, on the rise of Buddhist nationalism in Myanmar since 2011, with anti-Muslim hate speech and communal violence in Rakhine State and elsewhere. It traces the historical links between Buddhism and the state, and explains the origins, laws, politics and social work of MaBaTha, the Association for the Protection of Race and Religion, and why it is popular. It assesses the risk of further violence and advises the government on how to respond.

edit.title: Building a Better Future for Rohingya Refugees in Bangladesh
edit.mDescription:
International Crisis Group Asia Briefing No. 155, published on 25 April 2019 after a visit to Dhaka and the Cox's Bazar camps. Eighteen months after 740,000 Rohingya were expelled from Myanmar, it finds that return is not possible soon, partly because of fighting with the Arakan Army, and that the camps face growing insecurity from militants and gangs and a ban on formal education. It urges Bangladesh to put a regular police presence in the camps and lift the education ban, with donors helping to pay.

edit.title: Caged without a Roof: Apartheid in Myanmar's Rakhine State
edit.mDescription:
An Amnesty International report from November 2017, based on two years of research with more than 200 interviews and four field trips to Rakhine State. It documents how Myanmar's authorities control almost every part of Rohingya life, including denial of nationality and documents, the failure to register newborn babies, travel permits, curfews and checkpoints, confinement in camps, villages and the Aung Mingalar enclave, and limits on health care, schooling, livelihoods and worship. It concludes that this system amounts to apartheid, a crime against humanity.

Year          : 2017
Language      : English

edit.title: Crimes against Humanity by Burmese Security Forces against the Rohingya
edit.mDescription:
A legal memo by Human Rights Watch dated 26 September 2017 setting out why the abuses by Burmese security forces against the Rohingya of northern Rakhine State since 25 August 2017 amount to crimes against humanity. It explains the legal test under the Rome Statute and shows the attacks were widespread and systematic, citing satellite images showing the near-total destruction of 284 villages and the flight of more than 400,000 people. It then covers each crime in turn, namely deportation and forced population transfer, murder, rape and other sexual violence, and persecution.

edit.mDescription:
A factual findings and legal analysis report by the Public International Law & Policy Group, published in December 2018. It is based on 1,024 interviews with Rohingya refugees in the camps of eastern Bangladesh in March and April 2018. It describes years of persecution in northern Rakhine State since 2012 and the mass killings, rapes and village burnings of the August 2017 clearance operations. It finds reasonable grounds to believe that crimes against humanity, genocide and war crimes were committed, and calls for a criminal tribunal.

edit.title: Ending Impunity in Myanmar
edit.mDescription:
A legal analysis by Fortify Rights, written after the military coup of 1 February 2021. It asks whether Myanmar's National Unity Government (NUG) can represent the country and give the International Criminal Court jurisdiction over atrocity crimes committed since 2002, including the genocide against the Rohingya. It finds that the NUG can do this by lodging an Article 12(3) declaration or by joining the Rome Statute. It includes a map and a chronology of atrocities and steps toward accountability.

edit.title: Flash Report: OHCHR Mission to Bangladesh

A UN human rights report dated 3 February 2017. It gives statistics and testimony on killings, disappearances, rape and other sexual violence, beatings, torture and the burning and looting of homes. It concludes that the violations very likely amount to crimes against humanity and forced displacement.

edit.title: From Elections to Ceasefire in Myanmar's Rakhine State
edit.mDescription:
A short policy briefing by the International Crisis Group (Asia Briefing No. 164, December 2020). It explains how voting was cancelled in much of Rakhine State in the November 2020 general election, and how Japan's envoy then helped arrange an informal ceasefire between the Myanmar military and the Arakan Army to allow supplementary elections. A Fortify Rights report on how identity documents have been used to single out and destroy targeted groups. edit.mDescription:
A Refugees International report from December 2022, based on a visit to Dhaka, Cox's Bazar and the Rohingya camps in October 2022, five years after the 2017 genocide. A 2017 report by the Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK), based on interviews in the Kutupalong and Nayapara camps in Cox's Bazar with Rohingya who fled the violence that began on 25 August 2017. edit.title: No One Can Protect Us: War Crimes and Abuses in Myanmar's Rakhine State
edit.mDescription:
An Amnesty International report from May 2019 on the fighting between the Myanmar army and the Arakan Army that escalated after 4 January 2019. Based on 81 interviews with Rakhine, Mro, Rohingya and Khami civilians, and on satellite images, photos and videos, it documents unlawful attacks on villages, arbitrary arrests, torture, disappearances, executions, looting and forced labour by the army, and abductions and other abuses by the Arakan Army. It includes maps and ends with recommendations, including an arms embargo.
Author        : Amnesty International
Year          : 2019
Language      : English
Publisher     : Amnesty International Ltd, London
Pages         : 46
File Size     : 1.8 MB

edit.title: No One Was Left: Death and Violence against the Rohingya in Rakhine State
edit.mDescription:
A Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) report from March 2018 on the violence of the 'clearance operations' that began on 25 August 2017. It combines six health surveys in the Cox's Bazar camps in November 2017 with patient testimony and medical data from MSF's Kutupalong clinic. It shows a sharp rise in deaths, mostly from gunshots, burning and beatings, violence against women, men, children and old people, widespread sexual violence, and refugees' fear of returning to Myanmar. The methods are explained in an annex.
Author        : Médecins Sans Frontières
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Pages         : 28
File Size     : 16.1 MB

edit.title: Overcoming Challenges: The Story of NGOs Serving Refugees in Klang Valley, Malaysia
edit.mDescription:
A working paper by Imdad Hussain for the MIT-UTM Malaysia Sustainable Cities Program. It looks at Malaysian NGOs that help refugees around Kuala Lumpur, where more than 90 percent of refugees come from Myanmar and many are Rohingya. Based on interviews with NGO leaders, Rohingya community leaders and refugees, it describes refugees' problems with documents, schooling, health care, work and language, the NGOs' difficulties with funding, government and trust, and the strategies they use to overcome them.
Author        : Imdad Hussain
Year          : 2017
Language      : English
Publisher     : MIT-UTM Malaysia Sustainable Cities Program, Massachusetts Institute of Technology
Pages         : 24
File Size     : 0.3 MB

edit.title: Paths to Justice: Inclusive International Justice in Post-Coup Myanmar
edit.mDescription:
A ten-page briefing by the Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK), written in May 2021 after the military coup of 1 February 2021. It explains the international justice options - The Gambia's genocide case at the International Court of Justice, the ICC investigation, the UN Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar and universal jurisdiction cases - and how the National Unity Government could support them. It argues that justice for the coup must also include the Rohingya, and recommends that the NUG restore Rohingya citizenship and include Rohingya representatives.
Author        : Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK
Year          : 2021
Language      : English
Pages         : 10
File Size     : 0.3 MB

edit.title: Policies of Persecution: Ending Abusive State Policies against Rohingya Muslims in Myanmar
edit.mDescription:
A Fortify Rights report from February 2014 based on leaked official documents - regional orders and guidelines dated 1993 to 2008 - that restrict the lives of Rohingya in northern Rakhine State. It explains the two-child policy in Maungdaw and Buthidaung, enforced birth control, marriage permits, limits on movement, household checks and bans on repairing homes and mosques, and how security forces enforce them. It argues these policies may amount to the crime against humanity of persecution. Unofficial English translations of the orders are printed in the appendices.
Author        : Fortify Rights
Year          : 2014
Language      : English
Pages         : 79
File Size     : 45.3 MB

edit.title: Prevent the Unthinkable
edit.mDescription:
A briefing by the Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK) on whether Myanmar obeyed the International Court of Justice's 2020 order to protect the Rohingya, covering May to November 2022. It explains the ICJ's July 2022 rejection of Myanmar's objections in The Gambia's genocide case, and documents killings, drone and artillery attacks, movement restrictions, arrests and aid blocks in Rakhine as fighting between the military and the Arakan Army grew. It warns of a repeat of 2017 and urges the UN and states to act.
Author        : Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK
Year          : 2022
Language      : English
Pages         : 36
File Size     : 0.4 MB

edit.title: Preventable Deaths in Cyclone Mocha and the Rohingya Genocide
edit.mDescription:
A briefing by the Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK), up to date to 23 May 2023, on Cyclone Mocha, which struck Rakhine State on 14 May 2023. It reports that at least 400 Rohingya died, most of them in the flood-prone internment camps near Sittwe where they have been held since 2012, and blames movement restrictions, poor warnings and blocked aid. It argues that these conditions are part of the genocide and breach the International Court of Justice's 2020 order, and gives recommendations to the ICJ, the UN and states.
Author        : Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK
Year          : 2023
Language      : English
Pages         : 30
File Size     : 1.3 MB

edit.title: Preventing a Lost Generation: Community-Led Education by Rohingya Refugees
edit.mDescription:
A four-page policy brief (PRIO Policy Brief 07/2019) from the Peace Research Institute Oslo. The team surveyed 27 education networks run by Rohingya refugees in the Cox's Bazar camps, with 373 teachers teaching nearly 10,000 children and youth. It describes who the teachers are, why they teach, how they value the Myanmar school curriculum, and their criticism of agency learning centres. It recommends that Bangladesh allow refugee-led education and that agencies work with these networks and seek recognised Myanmar exams.
Author        : Jessica Olney, Nurul Haque, Roshid Mubarak, Marte Nilsen, Ingebjørg Finnbakk, Gudrun Østby and Kendra Dupuy (PRIO)
Year          : 2019
Language      : English
Publisher     : Peace Research Institute Oslo (PRIO), Oslo
ISBN          : 978-82-343-0009-7 (online), 978-82-343-0008-0 (print)
Pages         : 4
File Size     : 0.2 MB

edit.title: Rape by Command: Sexual Violence by the Myanmar Army
edit.mDescription:
A report by the Kaladan Press Network, first published in February 2018, with Razia Sultana as chief researcher. Based on testimony from 36 refugees, including eight rape survivors, it documents the rape of well over 300 Rohingya women and girls by Myanmar soldiers in at least 17 villages of Maungdaw and northern Buthidaung and in Maungdaw town during the 2017 clearance operation, including the Tula Toli massacre. It describes patterns of gang rape, mutilation and killing, includes a map, a list of incidents and a survivor's full account, and gives recommendations.
Author        : Razia Sultana (Kaladan Press Network)
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Publisher     : Kaladan Press Network, Chittagong
Pages         : 62
File Size     : 0.7 MB

edit.title: Refugee Movements in South-East Asia, 2018 – June 2019
edit.mDescription:
A UNHCR report from its Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific on refugee movements in South-East Asia from January 2018 to June 2019, most of them Rohingya. It covers new arrivals in Bangladesh, the small return of boat journeys across the Bay of Bengal and Andaman Sea (at least 1,597 people), interceptions at sea, abuse by smugglers, deaths, and detention, with refugees' own accounts. It ends with recommendations to states on root causes, rescue at sea, access to asylum and ending child detention.
Author        : UNHCR
Year          : 2019
Language      : English
Pages         : 20
File Size     : 1.3 MB

edit.title: Remaking Rakhine State
edit.mDescription:
A two-page Amnesty International public statement dated 12 March 2018, delivered at the 37th session of the UN Human Rights Council. It says the security forces' campaign against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State amounts to crimes against humanity, notes satellite images showing new security bases built over burned Rohingya villages, and calls for an accountability mechanism and a body in Cox's Bazar to collect evidence for future trials.
Author        : Amnesty International
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Pages         : 2
File Size     : 0.2 MB

edit.title: Report of the Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Myanmar (A/HRC/39/64)
edit.mDescription:
The summary report of the UN fact-finding mission on Myanmar (chaired by Marzuki Darusman), issued on 12 September 2018 for the 39th session of the Human Rights Council. It covers Kachin, Rakhine and Shan States since 2011 - the oppression of the Rohingya, the 2012 violence, the 2016 and 2017 'clearance operations' with mass killings, gang rape and village burning, and abuses in the northern conflicts. It finds that senior generals should be investigated and prosecuted for genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes, and recommends an international justice mechanism.
Author        : UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Myanmar
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Publisher     : United Nations Human Rights Council
Pages         : 21
File Size     : 0.5 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Christians Persecution
edit.mDescription:
A short two-page account of the small Rohingya Christian community, which it says makes up about 0.75 percent of Rohingya and grew mainly in Buthidaung. It describes threats from both the Myanmar military and radical Muslims, and lists dated incidents in the Kutupalong camp in Bangladesh from 2017 to January 2020 - arrests, beatings, attacks on homes and churches, abductions and forced conversions that the author blames on ARSA and others, and police inaction.
Author        : Mohammad Sadeq
Year          : 2023
Language      : English
Pages         : 2
File Size     : 0.2 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Crisis: A Summary of Findings from Six Pooled Surveys
edit.mDescription:
A Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) project update from 9 December 2017, saved from the MSF website. It summarises six mortality surveys of 2,434 households in the Kutupalong, Balukhali and Tasnimarkhola settlements in Cox's Bazar in November 2017. In the month after 25 August 2017, death rates were 13 times higher than before, mostly from shooting, burning and beatings. MSF estimates that 11,393 people died in that month, 8,170 of them violently, including 1,247 children under five.
Author        : Médecins Sans Frontières
Year          : 2017
Language      : English
Pages         : 5
File Size     : 0.2 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Genocide Day Bulletin 2024
edit.mDescription:
A special magazine issue published by the Arakan Rohingya National Alliance (ARNA) for Rohingya Genocide Remembrance Day, 25 August 2024. It has four articles - Nurul Islam on the history of the genocide and the court cases, Aman Ullah on the legal basis of the 'clearance operations', Nay San Lwin on the Arakan Army's abuses against Rohingya in 2024, and Mohammad Habib Ullah on the silence of the international community. The writers argue that the Arakan Army is continuing the military's persecution. It ends with ARNA's remembrance day observance.
Author        : Arakan Rohingya National Alliance
Year          : 2024
Language      : English
Pages         : 22
File Size     : 9.0 MB

edit.title: Sold Like Fish: Crimes against Humanity, Mass Graves, and Human Trafficking from Myanmar and Bangladesh to Malaysia
edit.mDescription:
A joint report from March 2019 by the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (SUHAKAM) and Fortify Rights, based on 270 interviews from 2013 to 2019, mostly with Rohingya survivors. It documents how a criminal syndicate trafficked more than 170,000 Rohingya and Bangladeshis by sea between 2012 and 2015, with killings, rape, torture and starvation on ships and in jungle camps on the Malaysia-Thailand border. It covers the Wang Kelian mass graves found in 2015, officials' testimony, signs of official complicity, and a legal analysis finding crimes against humanity.
Author        : SUHAKAM and Fortify Rights
Year          : 2019
Language      : English
Pages         : 124
File Size     : 14.8 MB

edit.title: Starving to Death: The Latest Phase of the Rohingya Genocide
edit.mDescription:
A briefing by the Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK) from June 2025 on hunger among Rohingya in Rakhine State. It describes how aid cuts - including the US funding freeze and World Food Programme cuts in early 2025 - left the 112,000 Rohingya in the Sittwe camps without rations, with reports of starvation, malnourished children and disease in Sittwe and Maungdaw. It also covers the regime's suppression of food-crisis data, the March 2025 earthquake, Argentina's arrest warrants for Min Aung Hlaing and others, abuses by the military and the Arakan Army, and the ICJ case.
Author        : Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK
Year          : 2025
Language      : English
Pages         : 44
File Size     : 1.1 MB

edit.title: Struggling to Survive
edit.mDescription:
A briefing by the Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK) dated 21 November 2023, covering May to November 2023 for The Gambia v. Myanmar genocide case at the International Court of Justice. It reports how Rohingya in Rakhine State were denied aid after Cyclone Mocha, kept in damaged camps around Sittwe and caught in renewed fighting between the military and the Arakan Army, and how refugees in Bangladesh face camp violence, food ration cuts and pressure to join a pilot repatriation. It argues Myanmar is breaking the Court's order and gives recommendations.
Author        : Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK
Year          : 2023
Language      : English
Pages         : 31
File Size     : 0.8 MB

edit.title: The Cost of Waiting: Intergenerational Impacts of Protracted Rohingya Displacement
edit.mDescription:
A study published by the International Rescue Committee on 30 October 2025, eight years after the 2017 influx to Cox's Bazar. Based on a survey of 500 Rohingya and host-community households, 30 interviews and 20 group discussions, it looks at access to education, health, shelter, food and work, the weakening of community leadership, relations between refugees and Bangladeshi hosts, and whether full repatriation is possible. It finds women, children and youth most at risk and recommends long-term policies beyond short-term containment.
Author        : Centre for Local Governance Discourse (CLGD)
Year          : 2025
Language      : English
Publisher     : International Rescue Committee (IRC), Dhaka
Pages         : 24
File Size     : 9.9 MB

edit.title: The Displaced and Stateless of Myanmar in the Asia-Pacific Region
edit.mDescription:
A seven-page UNHCR overview from January 2021 of the 1.9 million refugees, displaced and stateless people from Myanmar in the Asia-Pacific region, about 1.6 million of them Rohingya. It gives figures and UNHCR's work country by country - Rohingya and other displaced people inside Myanmar, the camps in Cox's Bazar (education, reforestation, Bhasan Char), Karen and Karenni refugees in Thailand, and refugees in Malaysia, India and Nepal - and boat journeys in 2020, with four priorities for solutions.
Author        : UNHCR
Year          : 2021
Language      : English
Pages         : 7
File Size     : 0.6 MB

edit.title: The Human Cost of Failure
edit.mDescription:
A briefing by the Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK) from May 2021, written ahead of Myanmar's 23 May 2021 report to the International Court of Justice in The Gambia v. Myanmar. Set against the February 2021 coup and its crackdown, it checks Myanmar against each of the Court's 2020 orders. It reports continued National Verification Card pressure, deaths from denied medical care, movement limits, forced labour, extortion by the military and Arakan Army taxation, and new building on the sites of destroyed Rohingya villages. It gives recommendations to the ICJ, the National Unity Government and states.
Author        : Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK
Year          : 2021
Language      : English
Pages         : 13
File Size     : 0.3 MB

edit.title: The Rohingya Genocide: Starvation and Forced Labour as Tools of Erasure
edit.mDescription:
A briefing by the Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK) from November 2025, two months before the oral hearings in The Gambia's genocide case at the International Court of Justice. It reports a UN famine warning for Buthidaung, food blockades and aid cuts in Rakhine and the Bangladesh camps, forced recruitment and forced labour of Rohingya by the military in Sittwe, and killings, disappearances and other abuses by the Arakan Army. It also covers the regime's planned elections and Argentina's arrest warrants, and recommends urgent humanitarian access and accountability.
Author        : Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK
Year          : 2025
Language      : English
Pages         : 43
File Size     : 1.2 MB

edit.title: The Rohingya Muslims: Ending a Cycle of Exodus?
edit.mDescription:
A joint report by Human Rights Watch/Asia and Refugees International from August 1997, titled 'Rohingya Refugees in Bangladesh - The Search for a Lasting Solution'. It describes the forced return of about 400 Rohingya refugees from the Cox's Bazar camps in July 1997, the history of the 1991-92 exodus and UNHCR's repatriation programme, new arrivals fleeing forced labour, taxation and land confiscation in Arakan, and the denial of citizenship under the 1982 law. It ends with recommendations to Bangladesh, Burma's military government, UNHCR and donors.
Author        : Human Rights Watch/Asia and Refugees International
Year          : 1997
Language      : English
Pages         : 17
File Size     : 0.2 MB

edit.title: The Rohingya Survey 2017
edit.mDescription:
A survey report by the XChange foundation, funded by MOAS, based on 1,360 testimonies collected by Rohingya enumerators in the Cox's Bazar camps in September and October 2017 from refugees who fled after 25 August 2017. After background on the Rohingya, it gives the methods, the refugees' villages of origin, ages and documents, their journeys to Bangladesh, and the incidents they reported - burning of homes, armed attacks and executions, sexual abuse, attacks on children - and who carried them out. Most said they would return if conditions improved.
Author        : XChange
Year          : 2017
Language      : English
Pages         : 37
File Size     : 4.2 MB

edit.title: The Social Atrocity: Meta and the Right to Remedy for the Rohingya
edit.mDescription:
An Amnesty International report from September 2022 on the role of Facebook's owner Meta in the 2017 violence against the Rohingya. Based on interviews with Rohingya refugees, former Meta staff and experts, and on internal documents leaked by whistle-blower Frances Haugen, it shows how Facebook's algorithms spread anti-Rohingya hate speech in Myanmar for years, and how Meta ignored repeated warnings in the years before 2017. It argues Meta contributed to the abuses and must pay remedy, including the education fund Rohingya refugees asked for, and sets out reforms for Meta and governments.
Author        : Amnesty International
Year          : 2022
Language      : English
Publisher     : Amnesty International Ltd, London
Pages         : 74
File Size     : 1.2 MB

edit.title: The World's Stateless 2020: Deprivation of Nationality
edit.mDescription:
The 2020 edition of the Institute on Statelessness and Inclusion's flagship report, published in March 2020. Part I surveys statelessness worldwide, region by region, including the Rohingya in the Asia-Pacific chapter. Part II, on deprivation of nationality, gathers essays by experts and activists - among them a comparison of Myanmar, the Dominican Republic and India - on citizenship stripping as a security and counter-terrorism measure, international law and country cases such as Bahrain and the UK. It ends with the Principles on Deprivation of Nationality as a National Security Measure.
Author        : Institute on Statelessness and Inclusion
Year          : 2020
Language      : English
Publisher     : Institute on Statelessness and Inclusion
ISBN          : 9789082836660
Pages         : 300
File Size     : 6.5 MB

edit.title: Tools of Genocide: National Verification Cards and the Denial of Citizenship of Rohingya Muslims
edit.mDescription:
A Fortify Rights report from September 2019, based on 628 interviews from 2014 to 2019 in Rakhine State, Cox's Bazar and Kuala Lumpur. It shows how the Myanmar authorities forced or pressured Rohingya, sometimes with torture, to accept National Verification Cards that label them 'Bengali' foreigners and deny them citizenship. It traces the history of citizenship denial from 1947, explains how the cards limit movement, fishing and work, and how aid agencies became involved, and makes 24 recommendations. Annexes show the card and a letter to the government.
Author        : Fortify Rights
Year          : 2019
Language      : English
Pages         : 102
File Size     : 10.5 MB

edit.title: Towards a Peaceful, Fair and Prosperous Future for the People of Rakhine
edit.mDescription:
The final report of the Advisory Commission on Rakhine State, chaired by Kofi Annan, published in August 2017 just before the 25 August violence. Set up in 2016 at Aung San Suu Kyi's request, the Commission describes Rakhine as a crisis of development, human rights and security. After a short history, it gives findings and 88 numbered recommendations on the economy, citizenship verification and the 1982 Citizenship Law, freedom of movement, displaced people, humanitarian and media access, education, health, security, justice and relations with Bangladesh. It avoids the words 'Rohingya' and 'Bengali'.
Author        : Advisory Commission on Rakhine State (chaired by Kofi Annan)
Year          : 2017
Language      : English
Pages         : 66
File Size     : 0.4 MB

edit.title: Two Settlements, Two Diverging Paths: Jobs and Labor Market Outcomes for the Displaced Rohingya
edit.mDescription:
A 2025 World Bank brief, prepared with UNHCR, comparing work and earnings for Rohingya in the Cox's Bazar camps and on the island of Bhasan Char, using surveys from 2022 and 2023. It explains how Rohingya work mainly through aid-agency volunteer and cash-for-work programmes and the informal economy, despite bans on formal jobs. Only about a third of working-age adults had work, with large gaps between men and women and many idle young people. Cox's Bazar offers more varied jobs, while Bhasan Char's isolation limits them.
Author        : World Bank
Year          : 2025
Language      : English
Publisher     : World Bank, Washington, DC
Pages         : 36
File Size     : 1.2 MB

edit.title: Voices Amid Strife: Rohingya Perceptions of the Arakan Army, War in Rakhine, and Justice
edit.mDescription:
A research paper (Myanmar Digital Research No. 14, June 2025) on how Rohingya see the war in Rakhine State since fighting resumed in November 2023. Based on eight months of media monitoring in 2024 and 40 interviews with Rohingya in Myanmar and Bangladesh, it reports killings, forced conscription, land loss, extortion and trafficking by the Arakan Army, the military and Rohingya armed groups, and how media coverage leaves Rohingya voices out. It also records hopes for coexistence and justice, with recommendations to the Arakan Army, the National Unity Government and the international community.
Author        : Tin Mar Oo, May Thu, Zar Ti Nwe Nu Aung and Hilary Faxon (Myanmar Digital Research)
Year          : 2025
Language      : English
Pages         : 55
File Size     : 1.4 MB

edit.title: We Must Prevent a Lost Generation: Community-Led Education in Rohingya Camps
edit.mDescription:
A PRIO Paper from 2019 mapping education networks run by Rohingya refugees themselves in the Cox's Bazar camps, where Bangladesh restricts formal schooling. The authors surveyed general education networks, private centres and madrassa networks across the Kutupalong, Balukhali, Thangkhali and Nayapara camps, describing their teachers, students, curricula, motivations and problems, with a history of Rohingya education in Myanmar. Recommendations cover using the Myanmar curriculum, including community teachers in the aid response, transparency and girls' education. An appendix lists each network surveyed.
Author        : Jessica Olney, Nurul Haque and Roshid Mubarak (PRIO)
Year          : 2019
Language      : English
Publisher     : Peace Research Institute Oslo (PRIO), Oslo
ISBN          : 978-82-343-0001-1 (online), 978-82-343-0000-4 (print)
Pages         : 49
File Size     : 1.4 MB

edit.title: Widespread and Systematic: Violence against the Rohingya in Myanmar
edit.mDescription:
An eight-page report of preliminary findings by Physicians for Human Rights, dated August 2018. It draws on a survey of leaders from 604 Rohingya hamlets in Maungdaw, Buthidaung and Rathedaung covering more than 916,000 people, 40 in-depth interviews and forensic medical examinations of 85 survivors. It shows that officials pressed nearly every hamlet to accept National Verification Cards before August 2017, then documents beatings, shootings, rape, burning of homes and mosques and attacks during flight, and calls for an international mechanism to collect evidence.
Author        : Physicians for Human Rights
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Pages         : 8
File Size     : 0.4 MB

edit.title: Witness to Horror: Rohingya Women Speak Out
edit.mDescription:
A report by the Kaladan Press Network, first published in February 2017, with Razia Sultana as chief researcher. It presents the testimony of 21 Rohingya women from nine villages in Maungdaw, interviewed in late December 2016 after fleeing the army's 'clearance operations' that began on 9 October 2016. They describe massacres, the killing or disappearance of their husbands, rape and the killing of rape victims, humiliating body searches, house burning, looting and being forced to give false testimony. It includes background on the Rohingya, maps of the villages and recommendations.
Author        : Razia Sultana (Kaladan Press Network)
Year          : 2017
Language      : English
Publisher     : Kaladan Press Network, Chittagong
Pages         : 27
File Size     : 1.9 MB

edit.title: Arakan Rohingya Union Narrative Report to OIC (30 April 2021)
edit.mDescription:
A four-page situation report dated 30 April 2021, submitted to the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation by Dr. Wakar Uddin, Director General of the Arakan Rohingya Union, three months after the military coup. It summarises the ASEAN leaders' statement on the Rohingya and Myanmar, new EU sanctions on junta members, apologies to the Rohingya by National Unity Government ministers, an Arakan Army statement, the eviction of settlers from Rohingya land in Sittwe and a decaying historic mosque. It ends with recommendations on citizenship, repatriation and the ICJ order.
Author        : Dr. Wakar Uddin, Arakan Rohingya Union
Year          : 2021
Language      : English
Pages         : 4
File Size     : 0.8 MB

edit.title: Impacts of the Rohingya Refugee Influx on Host Communities
edit.mDescription:
A United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) study from November 2018 on how the 2017 Rohingya influx affected Bangladeshi host communities in Ukhia and Teknaf, Cox's Bazar. Using household surveys and economic modelling, it describes the area before the influx, then measures effects on prices, wages, poverty, farming, fishing and the environment, on public services such as roads, water, health and schools, on safety nets and on social cohesion. It reviews existing aid and proposes programmes and income-support schemes for host communities and work schemes for refugees.
Author        : UNDP
Year          : 2018
Language      : English
Publisher     : United Nations Development Programme, Dhaka
Pages         : 224
File Size     : 49.5 MB

edit.title: Metasynthesis: DEC Rohingya Refugee Crisis Response – Lessons Learned Report
edit.mDescription:
A lessons-learned report from June 2020 by Charlotte Heward and Michael Carrier of the French think tank Groupe URD, reviewing the UK Disasters Emergency Committee's two-year response to the Rohingya refugee crisis in Cox's Bazar, carried out by 13 member charities from 2017. It summarises what was funded - food, water, sanitation, shelter, health and protection - and draws lessons on the effects, on host communities and the environment, on coordination with the Bangladesh government and local NGOs, and on involving refugees, with key recommendations for future emergencies.
Author        : Charlotte Heward and Michael Carrier (Groupe URD)
Year          : 2020
Language      : English
Pages         : 64
File Size     : 10.1 MB

edit.title: Village Tracts of Pauktaw Township, Rakhine State (Map)
edit.mDescription:
A one-page A3 map made by the Myanmar Information Management Unit (MIMU), dated 22 November 2011 (Map ID MIMU250v01). It shows the boundaries and English names of the village tracts of Pauktaw Township in Rakhine State, with Pauktaw town, roads, rivers and the neighbouring townships of Sittwe, Ponnagyun, Mrauk-U, Minbya and Myebon, plus a small locator map of Rakhine. It helps readers find places named in reports about central Rakhine.
Author        : Myanmar Information Management Unit (MIMU)
Year          : 2011
Language      : English
Pages         : 1
File Size     : 0.5 MB

edit.title: Rohingya The forgotten People
edit.mDescription:
An illustrated 14-page aid proposal by MAPIM, a Malaysian coalition of Islamic organisations. After introducing MAPIM, its leaders and its regional coordinators, it sets out three planned projects with budgets - a Ramadan food appeal in July 2013 for about 95,000 Rohingya in Arakan, Bangladesh and Thailand, a 'Peace Village' with shelters, a clinic, school and mosque for 2,000 displaced families near Sittwe, and relief, health care and schooling for Rohingya refugees in Malaysia, Thailand and Bangladesh. It ends with an implementation plan that seeks OIC support.
Author        : Malaysian Consultative Council of Islamic Organization (MAPIM)
Year          : 2013
Language      : English
Publisher     : MAPIM, Ipoh, Perak
Pages         : 14
File Size     : 2.6 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Class One
edit.mDescription:
A Rohingya reading textbook for school pupils, written in the Hanifi script and produced by the Burma Rohingya Zuban Committee. After a foreword and a contents page listing 21 lessons, each lesson has an illustrated reading passage, including animal fables such as the fox and the stork, family, food, school and daily life. Every lesson is followed by exercises with questions, fill-in-the-blanks and word matching, and the book ends with a poem.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Publisher     : Burma Rohingya Zuban Committee
Pages         : 57
File Size     : 15.4 MB

edit.title: Serak Magazine
edit.mDescription:
An issue of Serak, a Rohingya-language magazine in the Hanifi script, dated 18 February 2016. Its articles are set in columns with photographs of Rohingya villages, boats and a street demonstration, maps of Arakan, and religious pieces that quote Arabic hadith. The issue ends with a chart of the Hanifi Rohingya alphabet, vowel marks and numerals with their Latin letter names, and back-cover photographs of Rohingya life such as traditional wrestling.
Year          : 2016
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 12
File Size     : 3.6 MB

edit.title: Tarana Rohingya
edit.mDescription:
A collection of Rohingya songs (tarana) and poems written in the Hanifi script. Each piece has its own heading and is set out in verses over 22 numbered pages, and some songs repeat a chorus line between verses. Small drawings decorate the pages, such as a group of singers, a field of grain, a peacock feather and a horse-drawn carriage. The back cover carries the seal of the Rohingya Zuban Committee.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 24
File Size     : 3.1 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Science

Then come regional maps of Asia and maps of every continent, each with typed tables of countries, capitals, area and population, followed by tables and charts of islands, lakes, mountains, rivers and oceans, bar graphs, a poem and maps of the hemispheres. All text is in the Hanifi script.
Author        : Mohammad Amin
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 50
File Size     : 21.5 MB

edit.title: Rohingya English Burmese Vocabulary (Vegetables)
edit.mDescription:
A short illustrated word list of about 60 vegetables, fruits, herbs and spices, set out in a table with the Rohingya name in the Hanifi script, the English and Burmese names, and a colour photograph. It includes chilli, onion, pumpkin, cabbage, maize, ginger, mango, guava and many more. The last two pages, in Hanifi only, are picture pages that list the days of the week and the names of the months.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script), English and Burmese
Publisher     : Burma Rohingya Zuban Committee
Pages         : 10
File Size     : 1.1 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Foro
edit.mDescription:
A first Hanifi Rohingya reader for children, made by the Rohingya Language Council with Mukti Cox's Bazar and Children on the Edge. After a foreword and a chart of the letters and vowel signs, each page teaches two letters, each with a colour photograph, the word it starts, the word spelled out letter by letter and a short sentence. The last pages have word lists for reading practice and practice with vowel signs.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Publisher     : Rohingya Language Council
Pages         : 20
File Size     : 2.3 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Qaida (2023)
edit.mDescription:
A full-colour Hanifi Rohingya alphabet primer (qaida) for children and adult beginners, issued by the Burma Rohingya Zuban Committee and dated 15 October 2023 on its cover. After a foreword and charts of the letters, numerals and vowel signs, about 25 lessons each teach one vowel sign or spelling rule with syllable tables, word lists and dotted lines for writing practice. Later lessons explain doubled and nasal sounds and loanwords, give short reading passages and poems, and end with letters of approval from religious scholars.
Year          : 2023
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Publisher     : Burma Rohingya Zuban Committee
Pages         : 58
File Size     : 8.1 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Tarana (𐴌𐴟𐴇𐴥𐴝𐴚𐴒𐴙𐴝 𐴃𐴝𐴌𐴝𐴕𐴝)
edit.mDescription:
The words of a single Rohingya song (tarana), typed in the Hanifi script over two and a half pages. The song is set out in short verses, and the same two-line refrain comes back after every verse, so it is easy to sing along. There are no pictures and no text in other languages.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 3
File Size     : 0.4 MB

edit.title: Rohingyar Akholbon Hota
edit.mDescription:
A collection of Rohingya sayings and words of wisdom (akholbon hota), typed in the Hanifi script and dated 2020. After a foreword and a short poem, about 27 pages set out dozens of numbered sayings, each followed by a short explanation of its meaning and use. A few explanations compare a saying with an Arabic proverb or an English one, such as No risk, no gain.
Year          : 2020
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 30
File Size     : 3.5 MB

edit.title: Shayeri Kitab (𐴐𐴥𐴝𐴘𐴠𐴌𐴞 𐴑𐴞𐴃𐴝𐴁𐴢)
edit.mDescription:
A book of Rohingya poems (shayeri) by a single poet, typed in the Hanifi script. After a title page with publication details and a foreword that quotes Arabic religious texts, it has about 16 poems. Each poem has a title, an opening couplet set apart in colour, and verses of rhyming lines, and ends with the poet's signature. The back cover shows books and a quill over a map of Arakan.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 24
File Size     : 3.5 MB

edit.title: Soyi Lofzo
edit.mDescription:
A spelling guide (soyi lofzo, correct words) for writing Rohingya in the Hanifi script. It is one long table of about 200 numbered common words. For each word it gives the headword, the accepted spelling or spellings marked with a star, and in some rows a note or an alternative form. It is a quick reference for teachers and writers rather than a book to read through.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 9
File Size     : 0.6 MB

edit.title: Tarana
edit.mDescription:
The words of a single Rohingya song (tarana), typed in the Hanifi script on two pages. It is written in groups of short lines, and an underlined refrain line is repeated after each group, ready for singing together, for example in class. There are no pictures and no text in other languages.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 2
File Size     : 0.3 MB

edit.title: Tartib-e-Nisab (ترتيب نصاب)
edit.mDescription:
A long table in the Hanifi script that appears to be a list of spelling corrections for a Rohingya school text. Its several hundred numbered rows each give a word as printed, two reference numbers that look like page and line, marks showing which vowel sign or letter is changed, and the corrected word. The first rows refer to the book's title and its first lesson. It is a working document for teachers and editors.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 20
File Size     : 1.8 MB

edit.title: 𐴔𐴦𐴔𐴣𐴌 𐴎𐴟𐴁𐴝𐴕𐴡𐴌 𐴐𐴠𐴀𐴌
edit.mDescription:
A single Rohingya poem, typed in the Hanifi script on two pages. It has five or six stanzas of rhyming lines, and after every stanza a refrain line printed in red is repeated, so it can be recited or sung together. There are no pictures and no text in other languages.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 2
File Size     : 0.4 MB
